karty.g: Actions a character or unit can take that change the state of the game.
karty.nz: Each agent needs a clearly defined set of actions that visibly change the game state, and the sets should differ between agents so that choosing who does what matters. Players must be able to see what an action does and why using it is worthwhile.
karty.yr: Elements have actions listed on paper, but the actions are the same for everyone or never matter, so nothing is actually done with them.
karty.rk: which actions each element gets; how many and how strong they are

karty.g: The player loses abilities they once had, for example as a punishment.
karty.nz: The loss must have a clear trigger (a failure, an enemy effect, running out of a resource) and noticeably shrink what the player can do. The player also needs to see how it can be undone or worked around, or it just feels arbitrary.
karty.yr: A 'loss' is announced but the player can still do everything useful, or it lasts so briefly that it is ignored.
karty.rk: which actions are lost; what triggers it; how long it lasts
karty.ik: <path d='M8 56l14-14'/><path d='M17 37l10 10'/><path d='M22 42l12-12'/><path d='M42 24l14-16' stroke='#e85d4f' stroke-width='6'/>

karty.g: The player improves something outside the game world, such as a rating, rank, or reputation.
karty.nz: There must be a player-level structure that can be improved, with improvements that really change which options are open or how strong they are. Players should be able to see progress and ideally choose its direction.
karty.yr: Numbers on a sheet go up, but they unlock nothing and change no decisions, so it is just a counter.
karty.rk: what can be improved; cost and pace of improvement; how much choice players have over direction
karty.ik: <rect x='6' y='8' width='38' height='48' rx='3'/><path d='M14 22h22M14 32h22M14 42h22' stroke='#c9a24a' stroke-width='5'/><path d='M54 54V22M46 30l8-9 8 9' stroke='#4fa83a'/>

karty.g: An unseen part of the game that stores the player's parameters and possible actions.
karty.nz: The construct must hold information that actually drives what players can do in the world (resources, abilities, units), and must be under player control. It needs a clear link to the game world to matter.
karty.yr: A player sheet or panel exists, but it only displays information and has no effect on what happens in the game world.
karty.rk: what data it stores; how it connects to units and the world

karty.g: A reward that opens up content or actions that were unavailable before.
karty.nz: Some content must be actually locked at the start and opened by an achievement, and the opened content must be optional and worth wanting. The gate must be visible so players know what they are working toward.
karty.yr: The 'unlocked' area or action was available all along, or it is forced on the player so it is not an optional access at all.
karty.rk: what is gated; what unlocks it; how soon new access arrives

karty.g: Goals whose completion is remembered beyond a single play session.
karty.nz: Needs persistent storage across sessions, goals that point at varied or unusual play, and visibility to others if they are to carry social value. Goals should require effort or experimentation rather than happen on their own.
karty.yr: Badges pop up for things everybody does anyway, with no persistence or visibility, so they change nobody's play.
karty.rk: how many achievements; how hard they are; how visible and what they ask players to try
karty.ik: <path d='M16 4h12l6 20H22z' fill='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M48 4H36l-6 20h12z' fill='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/><circle cx='32' cy='42' r='15' fill='#c9a24a'/><path d='M32 34l2.5 5 5.5.8-4 4 1 5.5-5-2.6-5 2.6 1-5.5-4-4 5.5-.8z' fill='#fff' stroke-width='2'/>

karty.g: A strong enemy has a weak spot, and hitting it is the easiest way to win.
karty.nz: The target must be really resistant to normal attacks, with one specific weakness that is much more effective. Players must be able to discover it (clues, experimenting) and have the means to exploit it.
karty.yr: A weak point is labeled on the enemy but normal attacks work just as well, so nobody needs to look for it.
karty.rk: how much more damage the weak point takes; how hidden it is; what is needed to exploit it

karty.g: The game limits how many actions can be taken per turn or per period of time.
karty.nz: The cap must be tighter than what players would like to do, so that they have to choose which actions to spend. It matters most in turn-based or tick-based play where the player cannot simply act faster.
karty.yr: A limit exists on paper but is so generous that it is never reached, so players never need to prioritize.
karty.rk: number of actions per turn or period; whether the cap is per action type or total
karty.ik: <circle cx='12' cy='32' r='6' fill='#c9a24a'/><circle cx='28' cy='32' r='6' fill='#c9a24a'/><circle cx='44' cy='32' r='6' fill='#c9a24a' fill-opacity='.0'/><path d='M56 10v44' stroke='#e85d4f' stroke-width='6'/>

karty.g: The player chooses actions in advance, and they are carried out later.
karty.nz: There must be a gap between choosing and execution in which things can change, plus a limited set or budget of programmable actions. Players need enough consequence visibility to plan but not so much that outcomes are certain.
karty.yr: Players 'program' actions but execution is immediate or nothing changes in between, so it is just ordinary choosing.
karty.rk: how many actions are programmed at once; which actions are available; time allowed to plan
karty.ik: <rect x='4' y='24' width='14' height='16' rx='2' fill='#2f6b8f'/><rect x='25' y='24' width='14' height='16' rx='2' fill='#2f6b8f'/><rect x='46' y='24' width='14' height='16' rx='2' fill='#c9a24a'/><path d='M19 32h5M40 32h5' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M8 14h48' stroke-dasharray='1 7'/>

karty.g: A hero's deeds change how other characters in the world treat them.
karty.nz: Characters or factions need defined norms and a system (a score or behaviour rules) that visibly changes how they treat the player after relevant actions. The reactions must carry real benefits or costs.
karty.yr: NPCs say different lines after a theft but treat the player exactly the same, so nothing in play changes.
karty.rk: which actions count; how strongly NPCs react; how visible and lasting the reputation is

karty.g: The player does not attribute other people's in-game behavior to their real personality.
karty.nz: Gameplay should depend on in-game skill rather than outside traits, with anonymity or minimal personal information and a welcoming theme and presentation. Players must have little reason or means to judge each other by who they are.
karty.yr: Usernames are hidden but voice chat or profiles still reveal identity, or the game rewards real-world traits, so people are still judged outside the game.
karty.rk: how much player identity is revealed; whether AI or anonymous play is used; how much outside skill matters

karty.g: Pre-designed events and challenges used to build the content of a play session.
karty.nz: Needs ready settings, events, characters and goals that can be used with little preparation, and ideally structure (quests, scenes) plus room for a game master to adapt when players go off-script.
karty.yr: A pile of lore and locations is labeled an adventure, but it has no goals or events for players to run into, so a group can't actually play it.
karty.rk: how scripted or open the content is; length; how many are linked into a sequence

karty.g: Game creatures and objects that seem to have goals of their own.
karty.nz: Elements need visible abilities and actions that look purposeful and respond to circumstances, not fixed predictable motions. Players need to see them change the world in ways that suggest an aim.
karty.yr: A game element wears a creature's face but moves on a fixed track, and players quickly see it as an obstacle, not an agent.
karty.rk: how adaptive and varied their actions are; how visible their goals are

karty.g: Software characters that play roughly like humans and take their place.
karty.nz: The AI must play by the same rules as humans, with a visible aim of winning, and work in the available modes (teams, drop-in). Skill level should be adjustable to fit the people it replaces.
karty.yr: A bot occupies a seat but plays passively or randomly, so it cannot substitute for a real player.
karty.rk: AI skill level; when AI can join or replace players; how predictable it is
karty.ik: <rect x='8' y='22' width='48' height='34' rx='6' fill='#d5d9e0'/><path d='M32 22V10'/><circle cx='32' cy='7' r='3.5' fill='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/><circle cx='22' cy='38' r='5' fill='#2f6b8f'/><circle cx='42' cy='38' r='5' fill='#2f6b8f'/><path d='M24 50h16'/>

karty.g: The player aims at a target and shoots.
karty.nz: Players need a way to point at a target and an outcome that depends on accuracy, with some difficulty from movement, distance or limited ammunition. The target must be clearly visible and the control precise enough to feel fair.
karty.yr: Shots auto-hit or snap to targets, so aiming is just pressing a button.
karty.rk: aim difficulty (target speed, size, distance); ammo count; hit tolerance

karty.g: Warnings about an important change in the game, like fuel running low or guards spotting the hero.
karty.nz: A clear trigger and a perceivable signal, plus a real consequence (enemies converge, a timer starts) so players must react. Players should know what raised the alarm and whether it can be stopped.
karty.yr: A siren sounds but nothing in play changes, so players ignore it.
karty.rk: what triggers it; how loud or visible; what penalty follows; whether it can be reset

karty.g: Animals, monsters, and other creatures whose behavior follows rules rather than player control.
karty.nz: The rules must respond to the game state and produce actions that look purposeful and relate to the player's goals (hindering or helping). Behaviour needs enough variety to avoid being solved at once.
karty.yr: Entities repeat a fixed loop regardless of what the player does, so they behave like scenery.
karty.rk: complexity and aggressiveness of behaviour; how much it reacts to the player; how many agents

karty.g: A silly or supernatural explanation for why the game world differs from ours.
karty.nz: The fantastic element must have visible consequences in the world and its gameplay (new items, abilities, enemies), kept consistent with the theme. Introduced mid-game, it should be explained by the story.
karty.yr: A mention of magic or aliens is in the backstory, but the world and rules play exactly like the real-world version.
karty.rk: how big a departure from reality; when it appears; how many new elements it brings

karty.g: Goal: line up your pieces or elements in a row.
karty.nz: Players must be able to move or place pieces, and opponents must be able to interfere, so completing the line takes planning. The line needs a clear payoff such as a capture or a win.
karty.yr: Lines form by chance with no player influence or no payoff, so there is nothing to aim for.
karty.rk: required line length; how pieces move or are placed; whether opponents can block
karty.ik: <path d='M4 32h56' stroke='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/><circle cx='12' cy='32' r='8' fill='#2f6b8f'/><circle cx='32' cy='32' r='8' fill='#2f6b8f'/><circle cx='52' cy='32' r='8' fill='#2f6b8f'/>

karty.g: The boundary is blurred, so it is unclear whether events belong to the game or to real life.
karty.nz: Game information must be hidden within ordinary media and activities, with several channels and imperfect information, plus puppetmasters who react to players. Players need to be able to mistake it for non-game content.
karty.yr: A game is marketed as 'alternate reality' but is clearly labeled and runs in one app, so nobody is ever unsure.
karty.rk: how well game content is disguised; number of media used; how much staff react live
karty.ik: <rect x='10' y='6' width='30' height='52'/><rect x='17' y='14' width='16' height='14' fill='#c9a24a'/><circle cx='25' cy='21' r='2' fill='#2a2a2a' stroke='none'/><rect x='17' y='36' width='16' height='14'/><path d='M44 58h16M50 24a8 8 0 1 1 8 8v4' stroke='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: Actions that benefit someone else rather than the player themselves.
karty.nz: Helping others must cost the helper something or carry no obvious reward, with no shared payoff that makes it simply self-interest. Players must have a reason (social or hoped reciprocity) to do it anyway.
karty.yr: A 'gift' action exists but pays the giver as much or more, so players just do it for profit.
karty.rk: cost to the helper; whether payoffs are shared; whether gifts can be returned
karty.ik: <rect x='8' y='28' width='48' height='28' fill='#c9a24a'/><rect x='4' y='18' width='56' height='10' fill='#fff'/><path d='M32 18v38' stroke='#e85d4f'/><path d='M32 18c-10-12-18 0-6 0M32 18c10-12 18 0 6 0' stroke='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: A player's resources may be at risk even when they are not playing.
karty.nz: The game world must keep running and allow harm to offline players' assets, with real losses possible. There should be no pause or protection for absent players.
karty.yr: The game claims offline risk but offline assets are protected or losses are trivial, so absence costs nothing.
karty.rk: how much can be lost offline; how long protection lasts, if any
karty.ik: <path d='M6 56L26 22l20 34z' fill='#2f6b8f'/><path d='M2 58h42'/><path d='M52 6a10 10 0 1 0 8 14 8 8 0 0 1-8-14z' fill='#c9a24a' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M60 38L44 46M44 46l1-8M44 46l7 3' stroke='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: Game-controlled characters reply in ways that can be understood in more than one way.
karty.nz: Responses need to be truly open to several readings with no signal telling which is meant, so players have to judge meaning. This requires some uncertainty to remain over time.
karty.yr: A line is vague in wording but the context makes its meaning obvious, so nobody is ever unsure.
karty.rk: how many responses are ambiguous; how much context clarifies them

karty.g: Consumable items without which a weapon cannot be used.
karty.nz: Ammo must run out and be refilled by effort (pick-ups, trading, reloading), so players have to ration it. Several ammo types with different effects add meaningful choices.
karty.yr: Ammo is displayed but is effectively unlimited or always at hand, so shooting never involves a decision.
karty.rk: ammo supply and cap; reload time; number of ammo types

karty.g: The game stalls while someone takes too long weighing the consequences of possible moves.
karty.nz: Appears when many options have predictable consequences and a player's turn blocks others, especially with high stakes in the middle or end of a game. It arises from player behavior rather than a direct rule, so designers can only make it likelier or rarer.
karty.yr: A game has many options on paper but one is clearly best, so nobody deliberates and no stalls occur.
karty.rk: number of options per turn; predictability of results; turn time limit

karty.g: Actions from which you cannot tell exactly which player performed them.
karty.nz: Actions must be pooled or hidden (shuffled cards, simultaneous play) so no one can trace the source, and the identity must matter to the outcome. Social channels must not leak who acted.
karty.yr: Actions are called anonymous but everyone can tell who did them from turn order or table talk.
karty.rk: how contributions are mixed; whether identities are revealed afterwards; what penalty exists for revealing yourself

karty.g: Power over a zone: who can move through it and which actions are available there.
karty.nz: Areas must differ in value, be contestable by several players, and give real benefits (resources, abilities) to the holder. Taking and holding must require effort and be possible to challenge.
karty.yr: Areas are marked as owned, but all areas are equal or no one can contest them, so ownership means nothing.
karty.rk: how many areas; how valuable each is; how hard they are to take and hold
karty.ik: <path d='M4 42l14-12 24 4 18 8-12 14H16z' fill='#2f6b8f'/><path d='M34 38V8'/><path d='M34 8l14 6-14 6z' fill='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: Open places in the game world where fights happen on their own or by design.
karty.nz: Open spaces must be bounded and contain attractions such as resources or objectives, with other terrain types around them for contrast. Players must be drawn there by what it offers.
karty.yr: An open area is labeled an arena but has nothing to want, so players avoid it and fight elsewhere.
karty.rk: size and openness of the area; what draws players in; how many entrances

karty.g: Reward or risk grows in direct proportion to the effort invested.
karty.nz: Each unit of effort must give the same increment, with no multipliers or thresholds. Players need to see the relation so they can plan.
karty.yr: The rule is called linear, but bonuses or thresholds are hidden in the numbers so the real curve is not linear.
karty.rk: amount of reward per unit of effort; minimum or maximum investment
karty.ik: <path d='M6 58V46h13V36h13V26h13V16h13v42z' fill='#c9a24a'/>

karty.g: Items that protect against damage.
karty.nz: Armor must reduce the damage taken in a measurable way, with costs or limits (weight, slots, class restrictions) so equipping choices matter. Combat needs to be dangerous enough that protection is valuable.
karty.yr: Armor looks impressive and has a high number, but damage is so small or armor so abundant that it never changes outcomes.
karty.rk: damage reduction per piece; who can wear which; weight and slot limits

karty.g: Rules depend on how close a real object is to a real place, detected by sensors.
karty.nz: Sensing hardware has to be reliable and tied to a clear game condition, such as delivering an item, and the sensing range and the thing that counts as 'near' must be chosen on purpose. A short delay or a required action on entering or leaving helps cover for sensor errors.
karty.yr: Objects carry tags or the place has a sensor, but the game never checks them, or the same result could be got by pressing a button, so carrying the object to the place means nothing.
karty.rk: sensing technology and range; which objects trigger it; delay or extended action on entering or leaving

karty.g: Players' game experiences are built differently, or do not repeat earlier sessions.
karty.nz: Players must have really different actions or goals, and those differences must matter to how they decide and play. The differences need enough balance that no side is plainly better, and variety should not run out in one session.
karty.yr: Players get different names, pictures or flavour text, but the same actions and goals, so everyone plays the same game.
karty.rk: how many aspects differ (abilities, goals, information, roles, start); how far apart they are

karty.g: Goal: players have tasks of different kinds that cannot be swapped between them.
karty.nz: Each goal needs a different path and a different payoff, with abilities fitted to the goals, and some check that no goal is clearly easier. Cyclic strengths between goals can keep fairness while keeping the difference.
karty.yr: Players are handed different goal cards, but all goals reduce to the same thing, like 'collect the most points', so play looks identical.
karty.rk: how much goal requirements and rewards differ; whether goals are assigned or chosen; how well they are balanced against each other

karty.g: Players receive different sets of resources, so each has their own possibilities.
karty.nz: Resource differences must change what a player can do, with trade, scarcity or access to keep it interesting, and enough balance to stay fair enough. (The source page is a stub, so this is a best reading of the name.)
karty.yr: Players hold different amounts of some resource that has no use or can be freely swapped, so the gap changes nothing.
karty.rk: how big the differences in starting or ongoing resources are; who gets what
karty.ik: <rect x='4' y='48' width='24' height='8' rx='3' fill='#c9a24a'/><rect x='4' y='38' width='24' height='8' rx='3' fill='#c9a24a'/><rect x='4' y='28' width='24' height='8' rx='3' fill='#c9a24a'/><rect x='4' y='18' width='24' height='8' rx='3' fill='#c9a24a'/><rect x='38' y='48' width='22' height='8' rx='3' fill='#c9a24a'/>

karty.g: Players begin the session with different capabilities.
karty.nz: Differences at the start must affect early choices and the likely course of play. Balance through playtesting, rotating roles or handicaps, and decide whether they are fixed, random or player-made.
karty.yr: Starts differ only in cosmetics or trivial amounts, so after a few turns no one can tell who began where.
karty.rk: how large the start differences are; fixed, random or player-chosen; compensation for weaker starts
karty.ik: <path d='M6 8v22M28 34v22'/><path d='M58 6v52' stroke-dasharray='1 7'/><circle cx='18' cy='19' r='6' fill='#2f6b8f'/><circle cx='40' cy='45' r='6' fill='#e85d4f'/>

karty.g: Players help each other at different times and need not see each other's actions.
karty.nz: Game state must persist between sessions, and one player's action must give a real benefit to another who acts later. Players need enough trust, so keep the number of steps and the timing of rewards reasonable.
karty.yr: A game has a shared goal or gifts, but each player's progress would be the same without anyone else, so nobody is really working together.
karty.rk: how many steps needed to benefit; whether rewards come together or separately; time limits

karty.g: Players do not need to play at the same time; each joins when convenient.
karty.nz: Game state must be kept while players are away, with turns or ticks that do not stall others, and ways to show who else is in the game. Handle waiting with long timers, recordings, AI or gifts left for others.
karty.yr: A game is called asynchronous but still needs everyone online at once, or the world freezes and nothing happens in absence.
karty.rk: turn or tick length; how long state persists; what substitutes absent players (AI, ghosts, gifts)
karty.ik: <rect x='4' y='14' width='56' height='38' rx='3'/><path d='M4 16l28 21 28-21'/><circle cx='32' cy='38' r='6' fill='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: Any minute of inattention can cost the player dearly.
karty.nz: Several things must be able to hurt a player at any time, such as real-time events, multiple threats or continuous goals, with a real penalty for lapses. Lull periods must be kept rare.
karty.yr: A timer or enemies are on screen, but nothing bad happens when the player looks away, so they can safely ignore it.
karty.rk: how many things need watching; penalty for inattention; real-time pace; time limits
karty.ik: <path d='M20 58L32 42l12 16z' fill='#2f6b8f'/><path d='M6 42h52'/><circle cx='32' cy='30' r='9' fill='#e85d4f'/>

karty.g: The game partly aims for the player, making targeting easier.
karty.nz: The assist must really change hit results, such as pulling the crosshair or bending shots, in the situations where aiming is hard. Tune its strength against skill and fairness in multiplayer.
karty.yr: An aim assist option exists but is so weak it never changes a shot, or it only shows a marker without helping.
karty.rk: assist strength and radius; type (reticle pull, bullet bend, lock-on); where it is active

karty.g: The game uses several separate screens, such as a TV and a phone at once.
karty.nz: Each screen must show information that differs from, or adds to, the main screen, such as private data or overviews, so that looking at it affects decisions. Decide whether it shows shared overviews or private facts.
karty.yr: A second screen only mirrors the main one or shows decoration, so no one needs to look at it.
karty.rk: what information goes on the screens; shared or private; number of screens
karty.ik: <rect x='4' y='8' width='38' height='28' rx='3' fill='#d5d9e0'/><path d='M23 36v8M12 46h22'/><rect x='46' y='20' width='14' height='34' rx='3' fill='#2f6b8f'/>

karty.g: Figures in the game world through which the player acts; their fate depends on the player's success.
karty.nz: One entity must be the player's main way to act and be affected, and its fate must matter to the player. The more defined the avatar, the more it limits how players can role-play it.
karty.yr: A character model is shown, but its fate doesn't touch the player's progress, or the player really controls many units, so the 'avatar' is only a picture.
karty.rk: how much personality and detail the avatar has; how tightly its fate ties to player success; one or switching avatars

karty.g: Computer-controlled characters notice everything important around them and react.
karty.nz: Agents must sense the relevant objects, agents and events and respond differently depending on them. Context-dependent reactions and memory make it more believable.
karty.yr: Agents look like they see, but they ignore pick-ups, other agents or events and follow a fixed script regardless.
karty.rk: what agents can perceive; sensing range; how rich their reactions and memory are
karty.ik: <path d='M32 32V6a26 26 0 0 1 22.5 13z' fill='#4fa83a' stroke='none'/><circle cx='32' cy='32' r='26'/><circle cx='32' cy='32' r='13'/><circle cx='46' cy='42' r='4' fill='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: Right after one session, players play again with roles swapped.
karty.nz: Players must actually play again with roles swapped, so sessions need to be short enough and scores easy to compare across rounds. Lobbies help when players are remote.
karty.yr: The rules suggest playing twice with swapped sides, but nobody does or no one adds up the results, so imbalance stays.
karty.rk: session length; whether scores carry across sessions; how roles rotate

karty.g: Non-playing people influence the session with advice and opinions that players hear.
karty.nz: Spectators must be able to see the game and talk to players, and players must care about their input. Drop-in play lets people move between watching and playing.
karty.yr: There is a spectator mode, but spectators cannot communicate or players ignore them, so no one is influenced.
karty.rk: spectator visibility; communication allowed; drop-in/drop-out possibility

karty.g: The player must finish a level and then return along the same path.
karty.nz: The game must detect reaching the far end and then require a trip back, ideally with something changed or earned so the return is not just repeated walking. No shortcuts back.
karty.yr: Players are told to 'go back', but a teleport or instant exit takes them there, so the return trip has no content.
karty.rk: level length; what changes on the return; whether shortcuts exist

karty.g: Players put tokens into a bag and later draw them back out.
karty.nz: Players must choose what goes into the bag and when to draw, with token types that really differ in value, so the contents change draw outcomes. Decide whether bags are personal or shared.
karty.yr: Tokens go in a bag but all are the same or are drawn without choices before, so bag contents don't matter.
karty.rk: token types; when tokens are added and drawn; personal or shared bag

karty.g: Players can remove or swap tokens in the bag without playing them.
karty.nz: Removing or replacing tokens must really shift the odds, with a cost or limit so it is a decision. Choose how many tokens and what kinds can be manipulated.
karty.yr: Players may remove tokens, but the effect on later draws is negligible or the action is free and obvious.
karty.rk: how many tokens can be removed or replaced; cost of doing so; whether draws are blind

karty.g: Rules that shrink the leader's lead so the contest doesn't end too early.
karty.nz: The rules must really give help to those behind or cost to those ahead, at the right game phase. Too strong and players feel effort is wasted; too weak and the gap stays.
karty.yr: A catch-up rule exists but gives such a small bonus that a leader still always wins, or it is only mentioned in the manual.
karty.rk: strength of catch-up; when it applies (early, middle, late); preemptive or corrective
karty.ik: <path d='M32 46l-9 12h18z' fill='#c9a24a'/><path d='M6 46h52'/><circle cx='24' cy='37' r='9' fill='#e85d4f'/><circle cx='52' cy='41' r='4' fill='#2f6b8f' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: Stationary objects in the game world that give players actions or resources.
karty.nz: Each base must provide something useful that is tied to its place, and be buildable, capturable or destroyable so that holding it matters. Position should create real strategic differences.
karty.yr: A building is shown at a spot but gives nothing different from anywhere else, so ownership changes no choices.
karty.rk: what each base gives; cost to build; whether it can be captured or destroyed
karty.ik: <path d='M10 56V24h8v6h8v-6h12v6h8v-6h8v32z' fill='#c9a24a'/><path d='M26 56V46a6 6 0 0 1 12 0v10'/><path d='M32 24V8'/><path d='M32 8h12l-3 4 3 4H32z' fill='#e85d4f' stroke-width='2.5'/>

karty.g: Several players team up against whoever is leading the session.
karty.nz: Players must be able to see who is ahead and must have ways to hurt or hinder that player together. Hidden scores kill the effect; open scores and interference actions support it.
karty.yr: The leader is shown on a scoreboard, but players have no way to affect each other, so nobody can target them.
karty.rk: visibility of scores; how much players can interfere with each other; hidden or open goals
karty.ik: <path d='M4 4l16 16M12 20h8v-8' stroke='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M60 4L44 20M52 20h-8v-8' stroke='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M14 58L10 34l12 8 10-14 10 14 12-8-4 24z' fill='#c9a24a'/>

karty.g: A character breaks an explicit or unspoken agreement with another.
karty.nz: Players must depend on each other through promises or alliances, with imperfect information and a real gain from betraying. Anonymous actions or traitor roles intensify it.
karty.yr: The game has a 'traitor' label or alliance rules, but betraying brings no benefit or is impossible, so everyone just cooperates.
karty.rk: gain from betraying versus cooperating; how hidden actions are; use of traitor roles
karty.ik: <g transform='rotate(45 32 32)'><path d='M32 4l5 8v24H27V12z' fill='#d5d9e0'/><path d='M22 36h20'/><path d='M32 36v14'/><circle cx='32' cy='54' r='3' fill='#c9a24a'/></g><path d='M48 44c3 4 5 6 5 9a5 5 0 0 1-10 0c0-3 2-5 5-9z' fill='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: A player stakes resources hoping to win on an uncertain outcome.
karty.nz: Players must own resources they can stake, and the outcome must be uncertain with payoffs related to perceived odds. Decide whether the economy is closed or open.
karty.yr: A bet is offered, but the payout is fixed and risk-free or the stake is trivial, so nobody weighs the choice.
karty.rk: stake sizes; payout ratio; when the result is revealed; optional or forced
karty.ik: <circle cx='32' cy='32' r='24' fill='#e85d4f'/><path d='M32 8v6M32 50v6M8 32h6M50 32h6' stroke='#fff' stroke-width='5' stroke-linecap='butt'/><circle cx='32' cy='32' r='12' fill='#fff'/>

karty.g: Players offer resources in competition for the right to make a purchase or trade.
karty.nz: Players need bid resources that are scarce and also matter elsewhere, a clear rule for who wins and a reward worth competing for. Caps or limited budgets keep it a real trade-off.
karty.yr: Bids are called, but resources are plentiful, so everyone can always outbid at no cost and nothing is given up.
karty.rk: type and amount of bidding resource; whether the bid resource is spent or returned; what the reward is
karty.ik: <g transform='rotate(-35 32 24)'><rect x='16' y='12' width='32' height='16' rx='3' fill='#c9a24a'/><path d='M32 28v24'/></g><rect x='4' y='40' width='22' height='8' rx='2' fill='#2f6b8f'/><path d='M4 58h56'/>

karty.g: Huge man-made objects hinting at powerful creators.
karty.nz: The object must be seen from far away and feel vastly larger than the player, with hints about its makers. It should be a notable landmark players move toward or can't reach.
karty.yr: A big model is in the background but is not noticeable, has no hints of origin, and is just scenery.
karty.rk: size and visibility; place in the world; how much is hinted about its makers; reachable or not
karty.ik: <path d='M24 4h24l3 54H21z' fill='#2f6b8f'/><circle cx='36' cy='20' r='6' fill='#c9a24a'/><circle cx='9' cy='45' r='3.5'/><path d='M9 49v9' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M3 58h58'/>

karty.g: A player gives false information to influence others' decisions in their own favor.
karty.nz: Hidden information and unpredictable players are needed, plus ways to send misleading signals and a payoff for being believed. Face-to-face play adds skill, but any communication channel works.
karty.yr: All information is public or actions reveal intentions, so a bluff cannot work, or a bluff costs and gains nothing.
karty.rk: how much is hidden; signals available; payoff and cost of being caught

karty.g: Tokens don't represent world objects but simply store data about the game state.
karty.nz: Tokens must correspond to values the game really tracks and be easy to read and update, with a choice of public or hidden. Too many cause extra chores for players.
karty.yr: Tokens are on the table but players track values in their heads or on paper anyway, so the tokens are only decoration.
karty.rk: what values are tracked; how many tokens; public or hidden
karty.ik: <rect x='4' y='24' width='56' height='16' rx='3'/><path d='M18 24v16M32 24v16M46 24v16'/><circle cx='39' cy='32' r='5' fill='#c9a24a' stroke-width='3'/><rect x='10' y='46' width='10' height='10' fill='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: Powerful enemies that must be defeated to progress toward the goal.
karty.nz: A boss must differ in how it is fought, via special abilities, weak points or phases, not just extra health. It should be placed at a point of closure and be foreshadowed.
karty.yr: A normal enemy is renamed 'Boss' with a bigger health bar, so the same tactics work and it feels like a slog.
karty.rk: boss health and damage; special abilities and weak points; number of phases or lives; placement

karty.g: Points the player spends to take actions.
karty.nz: Points must be scarce enough that players have to choose, actions must cost different amounts, and replenishment must be set clearly. If everything is affordable, there is no budget.
karty.yr: Points are shown, but they are so many and refill so fast that no choice is ever limited by them.
karty.rk: points per turn or period; cost per action; refill rate; cap
karty.ik: <circle cx='13' cy='20' r='7' fill='#c9a24a'/><circle cx='32' cy='20' r='7' fill='#c9a24a'/><circle cx='51' cy='20' r='7' fill='#c9a24a'/><circle cx='13' cy='44' r='7' fill='#c9a24a'/><circle cx='32' cy='44' r='7' stroke-dasharray='3 5'/><circle cx='51' cy='44' r='7' stroke-dasharray='3 5'/>

karty.g: Abstract objects that define the point from which the game world is seen.
karty.nz: The camera type (follow or fixed, over-shoulder or overhead) must be chosen to match what players need to see, and control must not burden them. It affects surprise and tension through what is hidden.
karty.yr: A camera is present but it is fixed to show everything or is so awkward that it gets in the way, and view makes no difference to play.
karty.rk: camera type and angle; player control or automatic; field of view
karty.ik: <circle cx='16' cy='11' r='6'/><circle cx='32' cy='11' r='6'/><rect x='6' y='18' width='40' height='30' rx='4'/><path d='M46 28l12-6v22l-12-6z' fill='#2f6b8f'/><circle cx='26' cy='33' r='7' fill='#d5d9e0'/>

karty.g: A chain of pre-designed game episodes played in order.
karty.nz: The parts must be linked by shared story, carried-over progress and connecting material, so they feel like one arc. Decide what state carries over between parts.
karty.yr: Levels are grouped under a 'campaign' title but nothing carries over and nothing links them, so they are just a list.
karty.rk: number and length of parts; what carries over; amount of story between parts
karty.ik: <path d='M10 50L30 34L52 14'/><circle cx='10' cy='50' r='6' fill='#4fa83a'/><circle cx='30' cy='34' r='7' fill='#c9a24a'/><circle cx='52' cy='14' r='8' fill='#e85d4f'/>

karty.g: A player stays in one spot of the world for a long time, waiting for something to appear.
karty.nz: Waiting must be cheap, and a spot must give a lasting edge (range, cover, a spawn or resource point). Powerful ranged tools and hard-to-reach spots help it appear, while safe zones and alternative routes limit it.
karty.yr: A nice-looking vantage spot exists, but it is easy to flank or the target never comes there, so no one stays.
karty.rk: strength and range of weapons; how defensible spots are; spawn or resource frequency; number of flanking routes
karty.ik: <path d='M4 54L28 12l24 42z' fill='#4fa83a'/><path d='M20 54l8-20 8 20z' fill='#2a2a2a'/><path d='M4 58h56'/><circle cx='54' cy='12' r='5' fill='#c9a24a'/>

karty.g: Goal: remove a game element or bring it under your own control.
karty.nz: Clear rules for who can capture whom and by what action, plus a real consequence for the loser (lost unit, lost ability, retaliation).
karty.yr: Pieces are called 'captured' but nothing changes for either side; they come back at once or the loss costs nothing.
karty.rk: which pieces can capture or be captured; the capture method; whether captured pieces switch sides or leave play
karty.ik: <g transform='translate(16 36)' fill='#2f6b8f'><circle cx='0' cy='-14' r='7'/><path d='M-5 -7L-9 14H9L5 -7z'/><path d='M-13 18H13' fill='none'/></g><g transform='translate(46 52) rotate(-80) scale(.8)' fill='#e85d4f'><circle cx='0' cy='-14' r='7'/><path d='M-5 -7L-9 14H9L5 -7z'/><path d='M-13 18H13' fill='none'/></g>

karty.g: Players themselves change the effects and properties of individual cards.
karty.nz: Modifications must be meaningful and cost something, with real choices between them, and cards must be reused so the investment pays off.
karty.yr: Cards have upgrade slots, but one upgrade is clearly best or the changes are too small to affect play.
karty.rk: how many modifications a card can take; their cost; whether changes are permanent
karty.ik: <rect x='14' y='8' width='36' height='48' rx='4' fill='#fff'/><path d='M32 46V24M23 33l9-9 9 9' stroke='#4fa83a'/><path d='M52 6l2 5 5 2-5 2-2 5-2-5-5-2 5-2z' fill='#c9a24a' stroke-width='2'/>

karty.g: Elements used to hand out various resources without showing in advance how they are distributed.
karty.nz: Decide what is printed, which card types exist and in what numbers; use shuffling or hidden hands so the randomness and secrecy matter.
karty.yr: Cards are used only as a menu or list, never shuffled or hidden, so a table would work just as well.
karty.rk: deck size; number of each card type; information shown on each side
karty.ik: <rect x='18' y='8' width='28' height='44' rx='3' fill='#2f6b8f' transform='rotate(-18 32 56)'/><rect x='18' y='8' width='28' height='44' rx='3' fill='#c9a24a' transform='rotate(18 32 56)'/><rect x='18' y='8' width='28' height='44' rx='3' fill='#fff'/><path d='M32 20l8 11-8 11-8-11z' fill='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: The game is easy to start, pause, and finish without spoiling the experience for oneself or others.
karty.nz: Short or pausable sessions, a gentle learning curve, low stress and little punishment or dependence on other players' behaviour.
karty.yr: The game is marketed as casual, but it demands long sessions, has harsh failure or punishes quitting midway.
karty.rk: session length; ease of pausing; difficulty ramp; amount of penalty and time pressure

karty.g: The player feels the game is testing their skills to the limit.
karty.nz: The difficulty must match the player's skill, failure must be possible but recoverable, and success must be seen as the player's own doing.
karty.yr: Enemies simply have inflated numbers, or the game is difficult through opaque rules or luck, so players feel cheated rather than challenged.
karty.rk: enemy strength; margin for error; difficulty levels or adaptive difficulty; pace of the ramp
karty.ik: <path d='M4 32h56'/><rect x='14' y='14' width='8' height='36' rx='2' fill='#e85d4f'/><rect x='42' y='14' width='8' height='36' rx='2' fill='#e85d4f'/><rect x='6' y='22' width='6' height='20' rx='2' fill='#2a2a2a' stroke-width='2'/><rect x='52' y='22' width='6' height='20' rx='2' fill='#2a2a2a' stroke-width='2'/><path d='M32 8c3 4 4 6 4 8a4 4 0 0 1-8 0c0-2 1-4 4-8z' fill='#2f6b8f' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.n: Changes in Perception of Real World Phenomena due to Gameplay
karty.g: After playing, a person understands real-life phenomena differently.
karty.nz: The game system must model the real phenomenon faithfully, or tie game state to the real world (location, real activity), and players must be willing to draw the connection.
karty.yr: The game has a real-world theme painted on top, but the rules don't model it, so players learn nothing new about it.
karty.rk: how closely the model matches reality; how strongly game state is tied to real-life data or places
karty.ik: <circle cx='18' cy='22' r='10' fill='#2f6b8f' fill-opacity='.35'/><circle cx='46' cy='22' r='10' fill='#2f6b8f' fill-opacity='.35'/><path d='M28 22h8M8 22L4 16M56 22l4-6'/><circle cx='32' cy='47' r='12' fill='#4fa83a'/><ellipse cx='32' cy='47' rx='5' ry='12' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M20 47h24' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: A system classing heroes as good, evil, or neutral by their moral stance.
karty.nz: Alignments must be linked to what characters can do or how others treat them, and breaking one's alignment must have an effect.
karty.yr: A moral label appears on the character sheet but never affects rules, NPC reactions or penalties.
karty.rk: number and axes of alignments; penalties for acting against them; whether alignment can be changed

karty.g: The actions chosen during play determine what kind of character one becomes.
karty.nz: Characters need abilities that change or get interpreted according to the player's choices, and the game or its group must register and remember those choices.
karty.yr: Character traits are chosen from a menu at the start, and nothing the player does later changes them.
karty.rk: how strongly actions feed back into stats, relations or story; how many distinct paths exist

karty.g: Over the course of the game, a character gains new skills and grows stronger.
karty.nz: Visible progress with clear triggers, improvements that actually change what the character can do, and some player choice in direction.
karty.yr: Numbers go up but the experience of play stays the same, since challenges scale in step and no new options appear.
karty.rk: growth rate; sources of progress; size of each improvement; amount of player choice

karty.g: Stages of a hero's growth; each new one grants and strengthens abilities.
karty.nz: Clear thresholds, a meaningful reward at each step, and a sensible number of levels, with content for those who reach the top.
karty.yr: A level number is displayed but nothing is unlocked or improved when it rises.
karty.rk: number of levels; points needed per level; what each level grants

karty.g: Numbers and facts that describe an individual hero, item, or other creature in the game.
karty.nz: Values must differ between entities and affect outcomes, and some of them must be changeable during play.
karty.yr: Entities have stats, but all are identical or ignored by the rules.
karty.rk: which stats exist; their ranges; how they change
karty.ik: <rect x='8' y='6' width='48' height='52' rx='4'/><rect x='16' y='14' width='28' height='8' rx='2' fill='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/><rect x='16' y='28' width='18' height='8' rx='2' fill='#c9a24a' stroke-width='3'/><rect x='16' y='42' width='24' height='8' rx='2' fill='#2f6b8f' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: A set of traits and properties that make up fictional people and creatures in the game.
karty.nz: They need a persistent identity with data that changes and matters, which players can identify with or role-play.
karty.yr: A named figure appears on screen, but there are no data or changes behind it, so it is just a skin.
karty.rk: depth of personal data; how much players can customise; how much the character changes during play

karty.g: Places in the world where the player's resources change while they stay there.
karty.nz: The effect must be strong enough to be worth a detour, tied to a place, and must cost something (time, risk, exposure).
karty.yr: A glowing pad is placed on the map, but the effect is negligible or the pad is on the route anyway, so nobody chooses it.
karty.rk: refill speed; size of the boost; number and placement of locations; exposure to risk
karty.ik: <rect x='16' y='14' width='32' height='44' rx='4' fill='#4fa83a'/><rect x='26' y='6' width='12' height='8' rx='1'/><path d='M36 22L24 38h8l-4 14 12-18h-8z' fill='#c9a24a' stroke-width='2.5'/>

karty.g: Channels where players exchange messages directly inside the game.
karty.nz: Useful channel types (local, team, global), a way to find the right audience, and rules about who may speak and what.
karty.yr: A chat box exists, but it is empty, hidden, or so noisy and mixed that nobody uses it for coordinating.
karty.rk: types and scope of channels; moderation or filtering; friend lists

karty.g: Places in the game world that mark progress toward the goal.
karty.nz: Placement along a route that matches the goal, clear signalling, and a real effect when reached (progress counted, order or area control).
karty.yr: A marker is visible, but reaching it changes no state, so skipping it costs nothing.
karty.rk: number and spacing; whether order is forced; how visible they are; what happens on reaching them

karty.g: Places on the map where the way into other areas can be blocked.
karty.nz: The narrow passage must be the main (or only) route, with few alternatives, and the surroundings must make blocking or holding it worthwhile.
karty.yr: A narrow spot exists, but there is an equally easy bypass, so nobody needs to pass it or defend it.
karty.rk: width and length of the passage; number of alternative routes; who controls it
karty.ik: <path d='M6 6l20 24v28M58 6L38 30v28'/><circle cx='24' cy='10' r='4' fill='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/><circle cx='40' cy='10' r='4' fill='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/><circle cx='32' cy='22' r='4' fill='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: A responsive reaction to clicking that is pleasing in itself.
karty.nz: Instant, noticeable audio-visual feedback for every click, and a chance to repeat actions in a rhythm.
karty.yr: Things are clickable, but the response is delayed or flat, so clicking feels like filling in a form.
karty.rk: feedback speed and strength; how often one can repeat; effects on combos and timing
karty.ik: <path d='M24 16v34l9-8 6 14 7-3-6-14h12z' fill='#fff'/><path d='M14 18H6M16 10l-5-5M24 8V3' stroke='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: Moments when part of the game state is removed or becomes unavailable.
karty.nz: Reaching them must actually remove or lock part of the game state, and players must see what is ending.
karty.yr: A 'level complete' screen appears, but everything carries over and can be revisited, so nothing really closes.
karty.rk: how often they occur; reversibility; how clearly they are signalled

karty.g: Items or information that hint to the player how to achieve a goal.
karty.nz: They must carry real information about goals, appear at the right moment, and match the game's setting.
karty.yr: Hints exist but are too vague, too late or say what the player already knows.
karty.rk: how explicit they are; when and how often they appear; whether they adapt to player struggle

karty.g: People who lead a team and give its members advice.
karty.nz: The coach must have actual levers (training, tactics, reserves) that change team outcomes.
karty.yr: A coach title exists, but the coach can't affect anything the team does.
karty.rk: scope of the coach's powers; how team development is controlled

karty.g: An action happens only if several participants each do their own part.
karty.nz: The result must really need more than one agent, with outcomes depending on coordination and a way for them to coordinate.
karty.yr: A 'team' action that one player could do alone, or participants who simply do their own thing in parallel.
karty.rk: number of participants; timing precision needed; how rewards are shared

karty.g: Each player builds their own card collection and draws on it to pick cards for a session.
karty.nz: Cards must differ in power or function, be acquired over time, and be built into decks, with new cards released regularly.
karty.yr: Cards are sold in packs, but all are nearly equal or a few dominate, so collecting and deckbuilding don't matter.
karty.rk: rarity distribution; how cards are obtained; deck size; expansion frequency

karty.g: The player gathers items or elements, aiming to complete a needed set.
karty.nz: Collectable items must be spread out so that gathering them takes effort, and the gathering must serve some goal or reward.
karty.yr: Items lie everywhere and are picked up automatically, with no choice or effort and no use.
karty.rk: item scarcity and spread; effort per item; what collections give

karty.g: Goal: complete a whole set of smaller goals.
karty.nz: A clear set with visible progress, items with effort or variety behind them, and a reward for completion.
karty.yr: A completion list is displayed, but finishing it yields nothing and the items are trivial to get.
karty.rk: set size; rarity of items; reward for completion

karty.g: Actions aimed at killing or defeating opponents.
karty.nz: Opponents with opposing goals, an action set with real tradeoffs, and meaningful stakes for winning or losing.
karty.yr: Fighting animations play, but outcomes are decided by stats alone and nothing the player does matters.
karty.rk: damage and health; range of weapons and abilities; enemy strength; penalty for losing

karty.g: A set of actions that together achieve more than each does alone.
karty.nz: A specific order or configuration must give a bonus clearly beyond the parts, hard enough to need skill or planning but discoverable.
karty.yr: A combo counter is shown, but the extra effect is tiny or comes from simply spamming one action.
karty.rk: bonus size; sequence complexity; timing window

karty.g: Goal: the player commits in advance to completing a task, as if by contract.
karty.nz: Taking the goal must be optional, with a real cost for failing or for giving up other goals.
karty.yr: A 'commitment' prompt that can be dropped at any time with no penalty.
karty.rk: penalty for failure; reward for success; whether goals exclude each other

karty.g: The game provides ways for players to send messages to each other.
karty.nz: Channels must reach the right people at the right time and fit the pace of the game, with ways to filter noise.
karty.yr: A channel is offered but is too slow, too noisy or unavailable when coordination is needed.
karty.rk: channel types; audience scope; delay; filtering and moderation

karty.g: Goal: complete a quest built around the player's companion.
karty.nz: Triggers that players can notice, goals that matter to the companion's story, and rewards that change the companion or the relationship.
karty.yr: A companion has a quest on the list, but it is generic, has no story link to them, and changes nothing about them.
karty.rk: number of quests per companion; triggers; rewards and effect on the companion

karty.g: Game-controlled characters that follow the player and help them.
karty.nz: A companion needs a real role: abilities or goals that cover what the player's own character lacks, and behaviour reliable enough that the player can count on it. If they follow and talk but never change what the player can do, nothing happens.
karty.yr: A character trails behind the player and chats, but can't be hurt, doesn't act, and the player's outcomes are the same without it.
karty.rk: how strong and independent the companion is; how many can be had; whether they can be lost or turn traitor

karty.g: Heroes and other entities have specializations that can be developed.
karty.nz: Entities must have uneven abilities that matter for real tasks, and a reason to divide work or to choose a niche. Choices should be meaningful and not obviously one-sided, so no single specialty is always best.
karty.yr: Classes or units have different names and icons, but their numbers and options are so alike that any of them can do any job.
karty.rk: how different the abilities are; whether specialties are fixed at start or chosen and changed during play

karty.g: Some resource in the game is gone entirely, temporarily or permanently.
karty.nz: Resources must be finite or consumed faster than they are replenished, and something must actually use them up, whether players or the system. The running out must change what is possible afterwards.
karty.yr: A resource is labelled scarce, but it replenishes so fast or is so plentiful that it never actually hits zero.
karty.rk: starting stock; regeneration rate; consumption rate
karty.ik: <rect x='6' y='18' width='46' height='28' rx='4'/><path d='M52 27h6v10h-6'/><rect x='11' y='23' width='6' height='18' fill='#e85d4f' stroke='none'/>

karty.g: It is hard to plan actions or understand what they will lead to.
karty.nz: There must be enough components, rules and options that interact, so that deciding or foreseeing outcomes is truly hard. The complexity must be in decisions, not just in bookkeeping.
karty.yr: Lots of tokens, stats and menus, but one option is clearly best, so there is little to decide.
karty.rk: number of components, rules and available actions; how much they interact; how much information is shown
karty.ik: <circle cx='22' cy='40' r='12' stroke-width='6' stroke-dasharray='3.4 3.4'/><circle cx='22' cy='40' r='10' fill='#c9a24a'/><circle cx='22' cy='40' r='3' fill='#fff'/><circle cx='44' cy='26' r='9' stroke-width='5' stroke-dasharray='3.5 3.5'/><circle cx='44' cy='26' r='7' fill='#2f6b8f'/><circle cx='44' cy='26' r='2.5' fill='#fff'/>

karty.g: Goal: prevent other players from learning the information they need.
karty.nz: Players need a way to hide things (hiding places, hidden information, decoys) and an opponent who actually searches or benefits from knowing. Without both, hiding is pointless.
karty.yr: A goal says to hide, but everything is visible to everyone anyway, or nobody is looking.
karty.rk: how much information is hidden; how many hiding places or decoys are available; how well opponents can search
karty.ik: <path d='M14 8h24l7 50H7z' fill='#2f6b8f'/><path d='M2 58h60'/><circle cx='54' cy='52' r='6' fill='#c9a24a'/>

karty.g: A passage is open only if a condition is met, like a key, level, or quest.
karty.nz: The passage must be blocked for real until a condition is met, and the condition should require something the player does or gets. The player should be able to see the blockage and learn how to open it.
karty.yr: A door looks locked but opens with a trivial action or no real requirement, or the player can walk around it.
karty.rk: what is required to open it; how visible the requirement is; whether it stays open or can close again

karty.g: A physical play space that can be assembled differently from session to session.
karty.nz: The area must be built from rearrangeable pieces or markers, and the changes must alter distances, routes or length of play. Someone must be responsible for setting it up each time.
karty.yr: The board can technically be rearranged, but players always use the same standard layout, or every layout plays the same.
karty.rk: how many layout variants; who sets it up; how much the layout can vary
karty.ik: <rect x='6' y='6' width='24' height='24' fill='#4fa83a'/><rect x='34' y='6' width='24' height='24' fill='#d5d9e0'/><rect x='6' y='34' width='24' height='24' fill='#c9a24a'/><rect x='34' y='34' width='24' height='24' stroke-width='3' stroke-dasharray='4 5'/>

karty.g: Goal: arrange game elements in a required order or layout.
karty.nz: The target arrangement must be clear, and there must be real obstacles to reaching it, such as opponents, hidden information, time or a puzzle. Progress toward it should be visible.
karty.yr: An arrangement is named as the goal, but it is reached automatically by ordinary moves, so it asks for no planning.
karty.rk: size and complexity of the pattern; how many elements; how hard it is to place them
karty.ik: <path d='M32 12L12 48H52z' stroke-width='2' stroke-dasharray='3 5'/><circle cx='32' cy='12' r='5.5' fill='#c9a24a'/><circle cx='22' cy='30' r='5.5' fill='#fff'/><circle cx='42' cy='30' r='5.5' fill='#fff'/><circle cx='12' cy='48' r='5.5' fill='#c9a24a'/><circle cx='32' cy='48' r='5.5' fill='#fff'/><circle cx='52' cy='48' r='5.5' fill='#c9a24a'/>

karty.g: The player adds or rearranges elements to create buildings or structures.
karty.nz: Building must have a material or cost, restrictions, and results that affect later play, such as defence, production or scoring. Players need real freedom in what and where to build.
karty.yr: Players press a build button and a fixed object appears, with no choices and no effect on the game.
karty.rk: cost and materials; build limits; how much freedom in placement
karty.ik: <rect x='6' y='44' width='24' height='12' fill='#c9a24a'/><rect x='34' y='44' width='24' height='12' fill='#c9a24a'/><rect x='20' y='32' width='24' height='12' fill='#c9a24a'/><rect x='20' y='6' width='24' height='12' fill='#e85d4f'/><path d='M32 22v6' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: Players stop growing stronger and begin collecting victory points.
karty.nz: Building up an engine must pay off, but score-taking must eventually be worth more than more building. Players need to be able to judge when to switch, and the game must end in a way that makes the switch matter.
karty.yr: There are build actions and scoring actions, but scoring is best from the start or building is always best, so no switch is ever needed.
karty.rk: how quickly building pays back; scoring value; game length or end trigger

karty.g: Game elements that use up resources.
karty.nz: Something must really be spent or drained, at a rate that matters to what players can do. Players must have to deal with that demand, by feeding it, controlling it or competing with it.
karty.yr: Something is described as using resources, but the amount is trivial or nothing ever runs short.
karty.rk: how much and how fast they consume; what they consume; whether players control them
karty.ik: <path d='M26 32L42.4 20.5A20 20 0 1 0 42.4 43.5z' fill='#c9a24a'/><circle cx='22' cy='24' r='2.5' fill='#2a2a2a' stroke='none'/><circle cx='52' cy='32' r='3' fill='#e85d4f' stroke='none'/><circle cx='60' cy='32' r='1.5' fill='#e85d4f' stroke='none'/>

karty.g: Game elements inside which other elements can be stored or hidden.
karty.nz: A container must limit or organise what it holds, through capacity, access or location, so that holding something changes what can be done with it. Players should have to choose what goes in and out.
karty.yr: A bag or chest exists, but it holds anything without limit and puts nothing in the way of using the contents.
karty.rk: capacity; access rules; what can be put in

karty.g: Game characters respond differently to events and items depending on the situation.
karty.nz: Agents must react to relevant conditions such as place, history or who is present, and those reactions must be seen to differ. This needs enough authored content or logic, or a human playing the agent.
karty.yr: Characters seem to react but use the same canned response whatever happens.
karty.rk: how many context factors are checked; how many distinct responses are written; human or algorithmic control

karty.g: A scene interrupts the current one to show important information, like a memory or a look ahead.
karty.nz: There must be a clear signal for starting and ending such scenes and someone with authority to call them. They must give information that changes how the current scene is understood.
karty.yr: A scene break is announced, but it just repeats what players already know and changes nothing about the main scene.
karty.rk: who may trigger it; how often; flashback or flash-forward; which characters take part
karty.ik: <rect x='8' y='24' width='48' height='32' rx='2'/><rect x='8' y='12' width='48' height='10' fill='#e85d4f' transform='rotate(-10 8 22)'/><path d='M8 36h48'/>

karty.g: A character replies in conversation taking into account everything currently happening in the game.
karty.nz: Replies must be chosen from relevant game state, such as who is speaking, where, and what has happened, using rules or authored dialogue per character or place. Players should notice that the replies fit.
karty.yr: A character has many lines, but they are picked at random or ignore what just happened.
karty.rk: how many state variables affect replies; how much dialogue is written; per-character or per-location variants

karty.g: Goal: keep part of the game state within set limits.
karty.nz: Something must threaten the held state so that it needs attention, and failing must have a consequence. The player must be able to tell how well they are doing.
karty.yr: The game says keep something above a level, but nothing pushes it down or failing costs nothing.
karty.rk: how long it must be held; how tight the limits are; how strongly the state is pushed away
karty.ik: <path d='M6 46a26 26 0 0 1 52 0z'/><path d='M19 23.5A26 26 0 0 1 45 23.5' stroke='#4fa83a' stroke-width='7'/><path d='M32 46L35.5 26' stroke-width='3'/><circle cx='32' cy='46' r='4' fill='#2a2a2a'/>

karty.g: Stationary world objects that provide actions available nowhere else.
karty.nz: A player must have to go to the controller to use it, and using it must have a useful effect on the world or on their abilities. Their location should matter so that fights or travel form around them.
karty.yr: A lever or console is in the world, but it can be used from anywhere or does nothing significant.
karty.rk: where they are placed; who can use them; what the effect is and its cost
karty.ik: <path d='M14 58V46h36v12z' fill='#c9a24a'/><path d='M32 46L46 16'/><circle cx='47' cy='13' r='7' fill='#e85d4f'/>

karty.g: Elements that turn one resource into another.
karty.nz: The exchange must have a clear ratio and cost, and the output must be worth more to the player than the input in some situations. Players need to decide when and how much to convert.
karty.yr: A conversion exists, but the rate is so good or bad that nobody ever uses it or everyone always does.
karty.rk: conversion ratio; speed; what goes in and out

karty.g: After use, an action is unavailable for some time.
karty.nz: The wait must be long enough to hold back repeated use, and the player must have other useful things to do meanwhile. The remaining time should be visible or learnable.
karty.yr: An ability has a cooldown so short that it can effectively be used continuously, or nothing else is worth doing while waiting.
karty.rk: length of the wait; which actions are covered; shared or global cooldown
karty.ik: <rect x='8' y='8' width='48' height='48' rx='6' fill='#fff'/><path d='M32 32V10A22 22 0 1 1 10 32z' fill='#d5d9e0' stroke='none'/><circle cx='32' cy='32' r='3' fill='#2a2a2a' stroke='none'/><path d='M32 32V10' stroke='#e85d4f'/>

karty.g: Players act together, sharing information and resources toward a common goal.
karty.nz: Players need shared goals or rewards, and tasks that really are easier or only possible together. They also need to be able to communicate and swap information or resources.
karty.yr: Players are put on a team and share a score, but each can win alone without caring what the others do.
karty.rk: how shared the goals and rewards are; how often joint actions are required; communication limits

karty.g: Items that differ from others only in appearance.
karty.nz: They must change looks only, not abilities, and be visible to others, with enough variety or rarity that players want them. Players should be able to choose, show or collect them.
karty.yr: An item is sold as cosmetic, but only one player sees it or it is not displayed anywhere.
karty.rk: number of variants; rarity or cost; how they are obtained; how visible they are
karty.ik: <ellipse cx='32' cy='48' rx='26' ry='7' fill='#2a2a2a'/><rect x='17' y='12' width='30' height='34' fill='#2a2a2a'/><rect x='17' y='34' width='30' height='8' fill='#e85d4f'/>

karty.g: Events in one game affect events in another, and they depend on each other.
karty.nz: There must be a real data link, such as a score, item or result, that changes the state of the other game. Players need to notice and care about the effect.
karty.yr: Two games share a brand or login, but nothing that happens in one changes the other.
karty.rk: which direction the effect goes; what is passed between them; how strong it is
karty.ik: <rect x='4' y='8' width='24' height='20' rx='2' fill='#2f6b8f'/><path d='M16 28v6M10 34h12'/><rect x='36' y='32' width='24' height='20' rx='2' fill='#d5d9e0'/><path d='M48 52v4M42 58h12'/><path d='M28 18c8 0 4 24 8 24' stroke='#c9a24a' stroke-width='4'/>

karty.g: Creating game items from other items or materials.
karty.nz: Crafting needs inputs worth gathering and recipes or choices whose products matter for play. It should cost something, like materials, time, skill or tools, and the result should be better than what could otherwise be had.
karty.yr: There is a crafting menu, but the same items are easier to find or buy, so nobody needs it.
karty.rk: recipe cost; crafting time; skill or tool requirements; how many recipes

karty.g: An especially severe outcome of random failure that an ordinary miss never produces.
karty.nz: The bad result must be clearly worse than an ordinary failure and happen rarely, from a defined random chance. It must have effects the player really feels.
karty.yr: A critical failure is announced, but its effect is the same as an ordinary failure.
karty.rk: chance of it happening; how bad the effect is; which actions are covered
karty.ik: <rect x='10' y='10' width='44' height='44' rx='8' fill='#e85d4f'/><circle cx='32' cy='32' r='5' fill='#2a2a2a' stroke='none'/><path d='M44 10l-8 14 10 6-8 14' stroke='#fff' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: Game rules are built to make the player think and doubt something.
karty.nz: The game's own rules and dynamics must model something in the real world so that players feel its structure and see it differently. The critique must come from play, not from text or the story.
karty.yr: The theme or story talks about a real issue, but the rules play like an ordinary game and the issue is not felt.
karty.rk: how closely the rules mirror the real phenomenon; how strong the feedback loops and social dilemmas are
karty.ik: <ellipse cx='28' cy='26' rx='20' ry='22' fill='#d5d9e0'/><path d='M42 42l14 16' stroke-width='6'/><circle cx='28' cy='20' r='5' fill='#2a2a2a'/><path d='M20 38c0-8 4-10 8-10s8 2 8 10z' fill='#2a2a2a'/>

karty.g: Strikes that deal noticeably more damage or give a special effect.
karty.nz: The chance must be low enough that it feels special but high enough to happen in normal play, and the extra effect must be clearly larger than an ordinary hit. It may depend on skill or weapon.
karty.yr: A hit is called critical and a number pops up, but the damage is barely different from a normal hit.
karty.rk: chance of a critical; damage multiplier or extra effects; skill or weapon modifiers

karty.g: Predefined random failures in combat that harm the attacker themselves.
karty.nz: There must be a small random chance that a failed attack has a real penalty, such as dropping the weapon or hitting the wrong target. It should be rare enough not to feel unfair.
karty.yr: A miss is called critical, but the result is exactly the same as an ordinary miss.
karty.rk: chance of it happening; how severe the penalty is; skill or weapon modifiers
karty.ik: <circle cx='22' cy='22' r='16'/><circle cx='22' cy='22' r='6' fill='#e85d4f'/><path d='M58 38L34 54' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M34 54l2-9M34 54l9-2' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M58 38l-1-7M58 38l-7-1' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: An unusual random outcome of an action with an effect not available from an ordinary result.
karty.nz: The special outcomes must be unusual, come from the dice or random process, and do things ordinary results cannot. Their trigger must be clear so players understand what happened.
karty.yr: Rare outcomes are listed, but they only repeat what ordinary successes or failures already do.
karty.rk: trigger chance or dice condition; size of effects; which actions can produce them
karty.ik: <g transform='rotate(15 24 37)'><rect x='9' y='22' width='30' height='30' rx='6' fill='#fff'/><circle cx='16' cy='29' r='3' fill='#2a2a2a' stroke='none'/><circle cx='24' cy='37' r='3' fill='#2a2a2a' stroke='none'/><circle cx='32' cy='45' r='3' fill='#2a2a2a' stroke='none'/></g><path d='M50 4l2.5 6 6 2.5-6 2.5-2.5 6-2.5-6-6-2.5 6-2.5z' fill='#c9a24a' stroke-width='2'/><path d='M52 42l2 5 5 2-5 2-2 5-2-5-5-2 5-2z' fill='#e85d4f' stroke-width='2'/>

karty.g: An action succeeds by chance and gives a special effect that would otherwise be impossible.
karty.nz: A rare random roll must give a clear extra benefit beyond normal success. The chance may be tied to skill or tools, and the bonus must be felt.
karty.yr: A roll is called a critical success, but it gives nothing extra over a normal success.
karty.rk: chance of a critical; size of the bonus; skill or tool modifiers
karty.ik: <path d='M32 4l24 14v28L32 60 8 46V18z' fill='#c9a24a'/><path d='M32 16l14 24H18z' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: An on-screen mark that helps aim a weapon or choose a target more precisely.
karty.nz: The marker must show where an action will land, with fixed or movable placement, and match how aiming really works. It can also carry accuracy or target information.
karty.yr: A crosshair is drawn on screen, but it is not where shots actually go, so it does not help aiming.
karty.rk: fixed or movable; auto-aim strength; how much accuracy or target information it shows
karty.ik: <circle cx='32' cy='32' r='20'/><path d='M32 4v16M32 44v16M4 32h16M44 32h16'/><circle cx='32' cy='32' r='3' fill='#e85d4f' stroke='none'/>

karty.g: One session is played across several different kinds of media at once.
karty.nz: Each medium must be given a distinct job that the others cannot do, and the media must be linked by shared game state or goals. Players need clear ways to move between media without friction.
karty.yr: A game with a companion website or app that only shows ads or duplicates information, so dropping it changes nothing in play.
karty.rk: how many media are used; how much each one contributes to the game state
karty.ik: <rect x='4' y='10' width='36' height='26' rx='3' fill='#2f6b8f'/><path d='M22 36v8M12 46h20'/><rect x='44' y='24' width='14' height='32' rx='3' fill='#c9a24a'/><path d='M49 50h4' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: A token showing whose turn it is.
karty.nz: The token must be clearly visible and the rules must say exactly when it passes. It is most useful when turns are long or players act out of turn.
karty.yr: A token that sits on the table but is passed late or ignored, while players still ask whose turn it is.
karty.rk: token size and visibility; the exact moment it is handed over
karty.ik: <circle cx='32' cy='16' r='8' fill='#c9a24a'/><path d='M24 52c0-14 4-18 8-22 4 4 8 8 8 22z' fill='#c9a24a'/><path d='M16 58h32'/><path d='M50 10l-6 6M14 10l6 6' stroke='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: Story clips during which the player can do nothing.
karty.nz: They must carry information the player needs and be placed at points where a pause fits, such as before a challenge or at a change of place. Their length and the ability to skip them decide whether they help or annoy.
karty.yr: A long cinematic that adds no new information and changes no state, which players simply skip.
karty.rk: length; frequency; whether they can be skipped
karty.ik: <rect x='4' y='10' width='56' height='36' rx='3'/><polygon points='26,18 26,38 44,28' fill='#e85d4f'/><path d='M32 46v10M20 57h24'/>

karty.g: Cards that let you draw new cards, so the player runs through nearly the whole deck.
karty.nz: The game needs deck building, cards that draw further cards, and a deck small or thin enough that cycling through it is possible. Costs and limits must keep the loop strong but not endless.
karty.yr: A few draw-a-card effects that are lost in a big deck and never let a player cycle it.
karty.rk: how many cards give extra draws; deck size; limits on plays per turn
karty.ik: <rect x='23' y='20' width='18' height='24' rx='3' fill='#fff'/><path d='M10 32A22 22 0 0 1 32 10' stroke='#e85d4f'/><polyline points='26 4 32 10 26 16' stroke='#e85d4f'/><path d='M54 32A22 22 0 0 1 32 54' stroke='#e85d4f'/><polyline points='38 48 32 54 38 60' stroke='#e85d4f'/>

karty.g: Harmful effects from actions or events that lead to bad consequences.
karty.nz: Damage must be tied to clear causes players can avoid, must be measured in a visible way, and must lead to a real consequence when it piles up. The amount per hit must be small enough to allow several failures.
karty.yr: A health bar that drops but is refilled so easily or so cheaply that taking hits never matters.
karty.rk: damage per hit; how much health there is; how often damage sources occur

karty.g: What changes in the game when a character dies.
karty.nz: The cost of dying must be big enough to make players avoid it yet small enough not to make them quit. Saving and reloading must be limited, or the penalty disappears.
karty.yr: Dying brings back the player on the spot with everything intact, so death is just a short animation.
karty.rk: what is lost on death; how far away and how fast respawn is
karty.ik: <path d='M10 56V28a16 16 0 0 1 32 0v28z' fill='#d5d9e0'/><path d='M26 24v16M19 30h14'/><path d='M4 56h56'/><circle cx='54' cy='40' r='5' fill='#c9a24a' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M54 46v4' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: During a session, players add cards to their deck and then play with them.
karty.nz: There must be a varied supply of cards with different prices and effects, and the cards must go into a deck that is reshuffled so that choices show up later. Players should be able to combine cards in ways that matter.
karty.yr: Players add cards, but they are all alike or so weak that the deck plays the same whatever is chosen.
karty.rk: card supply and variety; card prices; whether cards can be removed
karty.ik: <rect x='6' y='14' width='24' height='34' rx='3' fill='#fff' transform='rotate(-10 18 31)'/><rect x='20' y='10' width='24' height='34' rx='3' fill='#c9a24a' transform='rotate(8 32 27)'/><path d='M50 38v20M40 48h20' stroke='#4fa83a' stroke-width='5'/>

karty.g: Sets of cards the game uses as a single whole; they can be shared or personal.
karty.nz: The set of cards must be shaped so that what is left in the deck gives useful information and chance. Players should be able to see or learn what the deck holds.
karty.yr: A pile of cards that is reshuffled every time, so no one can track anything and the order is irrelevant.
karty.rk: number and mix of cards; one shared deck or one per player
karty.ik: <rect x='6' y='18' width='30' height='40' rx='3' fill='#fff'/><rect x='13' y='12' width='30' height='40' rx='3' fill='#fff'/><rect x='20' y='6' width='30' height='40' rx='3' fill='#2f6b8f'/><path d='M35 17l7 9-7 9-7-9z' fill='#c9a24a' stroke-width='2'/>

karty.g: An event after which an ability works worse than before.
karty.nz: The reduction must visibly change what the player can do and be tied to a cause the player understands. It should usually be limited in time or reversible, or it becomes a dead end.
karty.yr: A penalty so small that the odds of success barely move, or one that is always cured at once.
karty.rk: size of the reduction; how long it lasts; how it is cured
karty.ik: <path d='M12 14v16M52 14v16M12 22h40' stroke-width='5'/><rect x='5' y='10' width='9' height='24' rx='2' fill='#c9a24a' stroke-width='3'/><rect x='50' y='10' width='9' height='24' rx='2' fill='#c9a24a' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M32 38v20M23 49l9 9 9-9' stroke='#e85d4f' stroke-width='5'/>

karty.g: A program, machine, or person who keeps records and manages the game's participants.
karty.nz: The facilitator must truly take over the work, such as hidden information, bookkeeping or fair judging, so that players need not do it. It must be reliable and trusted.
karty.yr: A computer or person nominally in charge, while the players still do all the tracking and rule checks themselves.
karty.rk: which tasks are handed over; who or what acts as facilitator
karty.ik: <rect x='12' y='20' width='40' height='32' rx='7' fill='#2f6b8f'/><path d='M32 20v-9'/><circle cx='32' cy='8' r='4' fill='#c9a24a' stroke-width='3'/><circle cx='24' cy='34' r='5' fill='#fff' stroke-width='3'/><circle cx='40' cy='34' r='5' fill='#fff' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M23 45h18' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: The result of an action or event appears not at once but after some time.
karty.nz: The gap must be long enough to be noticed and the effect must still matter when it lands. Whether players can see when it will happen decides if it brings planning or suspense.
karty.yr: A delay of a moment that players do not notice, or an effect that no longer matters when it arrives.
karty.rk: length of the delay; whether the timing is shown
karty.ik: <circle cx='26' cy='38' r='20' fill='#2a2a2a'/><path d='M40 22c4-4 6-6 10-6'/><circle cx='54' cy='12' r='5' fill='#c9a24a' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M16 32c2-4 4-5 7-5' stroke='#fff' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: You help others now, expecting the favor to be returned later.
karty.nz: Players must be able to help one another at a cost to themselves, without a guaranteed immediate payback, and meet again later so that returning is possible. Trust and the chance of betrayal must be real.
karty.yr: A gift button that gives help to anyone for free, so there is no cost, no trust and nothing to repay.
karty.rk: cost of helping; how likely and how soon players meet again; whether repayment is enforced

karty.g: Goal: move a game item to a specified object or place.
karty.nz: The object and the destination must both be specific, the trip must have some difficulty or opposition, and the delivery must be recognized by the game. The way there should require real movement.
karty.yr: An item that appears at the destination or is handed over by a menu, so no trip is made.
karty.rk: distance; what opposes the trip; how many items must be delivered
karty.ik: <rect x='4' y='36' width='16' height='16' rx='2' fill='#c9a24a'/><path d='M12 36v16' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M24 36c8-14 14-14 22-12' stroke-dasharray='1 7'/><path d='M52 58V10'/><path d='M52 10l10 6-10 6z' fill='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M44 58h16'/>

karty.g: Items that can be broken or destroyed.
karty.nz: Players must have a means and a reason to break the objects, and the breaking must change the game state, such as opening a path or giving loot. The object needs a visible durability.
karty.yr: Scenery that looks breakable but is not, or whose destruction changes nothing.
karty.rk: durability; what destroys it; whether it comes back
karty.ik: <rect x='6' y='14' width='38' height='40' rx='2' fill='#c9a24a'/><path d='M28 14l-8 12 10 6-8 12 4 10' stroke-width='3'/><polygon points='50,8 60,12 54,20' fill='#c9a24a' stroke-width='3'/><polygon points='50,34 60,36 56,46' fill='#c9a24a' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: The player knows exactly as much as one particular hero does.
