karty.nz: The game must truly limit what the player knows to what their one character perceives, and give clues through the world. It works best with a single player.
karty.yr: The player controls one character but the interface shows information the character could not know.
karty.rk: how much the character knows; how clues are spread over the game
karty.ik: <path d='M18 38c0-18 5-26 14-26s14 8 14 26z' fill='#d5d9e0'/><path d='M18 32c9 4 19 4 28 0' stroke='#e85d4f' stroke-width='5'/><ellipse cx='32' cy='42' rx='28' ry='8' fill='#d5d9e0'/><path d='M14 56h36' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: Items wear out from active use.
karty.nz: Wear must actually reduce an item's usefulness, and players must be able to fix, replace or manage items so that using them is a choice. The speed of wear must be noticeable but fair.
karty.yr: A durability bar that wears so slowly, or is repaired so cheaply, that players never think about it.
karty.rk: wear per use; repair cost; what happens at zero durability

karty.g: The game helps estimate how likely a planned action is to succeed or fail.
karty.nz: Actions must have consequences players can predict, and the game must give enough information or experience to let them estimate the odds. The estimate can be a little wrong but must be usable.
karty.yr: Odds are shown as a number that has no link to what really happens, so players can't judge anything from it.
karty.rk: how much information on odds is shown; how much hidden randomness there is
karty.ik: <circle cx='32' cy='30' r='22'/><path d='M32 30V8A22 22 0 1 1 10 30z' fill='#4fa83a'/><path d='M32 30l14-14' stroke-width='3'/><circle cx='32' cy='30' r='3' fill='#2a2a2a' stroke='none'/><path d='M12 60h40' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: A set amount of game time needed for an event to produce its main effect.
karty.nz: The time must be fixed and known and must be long enough to make players plan around it. Showing progress makes waiting readable.
karty.yr: A timer so short or so skippable that players never have to wait or plan.
karty.rk: length of the time; whether it blocks other actions; whether progress is shown

karty.g: Success depends on hand and eye skill rather than calculation.
karty.nz: The game must run in real time with quick, low-lag feedback, and outcomes must depend on how precisely the player acts. The challenge should fit what players can learn to do.
karty.yr: Actions that look like they need aiming or timing, but an assist makes them succeed whatever the player does.
karty.rk: required speed and precision; size of the target or timing window; lag
karty.ik: <rect x='6' y='44' width='52' height='14' rx='5' fill='#2f6b8f'/><path d='M32 44V24' stroke-width='6'/><circle cx='32' cy='16' r='10' fill='#e85d4f'/><circle cx='50' cy='38' r='0.5' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: Conversations inside the game world that the game system controls.
karty.nz: Replies must lead somewhere, giving information or changing the game state, and the system must handle what players can say. The choices should fit the characters.
karty.yr: A conversation tree where every option leads to the same answer and nothing changes.
karty.rk: number of branches; how choices affect the game state

karty.g: Physical cubes that give a random outcome from a set range, most often equally likely.
karty.nz: The kind and number of dice must match what is being decided, and outcomes must actually affect the game. Players can then learn the odds and use them.
karty.yr: Rolls that are ignored or overridden, so the result never matters.
karty.rk: type and number of dice; what the roll decides
karty.ik: <rect x='10' y='10' width='44' height='44' rx='9' fill='#fff' transform='rotate(-10 32 32)'/><g fill='#e85d4f' stroke='none' transform='rotate(-10 32 32)'><circle cx='22' cy='22' r='4'/><circle cx='42' cy='22' r='4'/><circle cx='32' cy='32' r='4'/><circle cx='22' cy='42' r='4'/><circle cx='42' cy='42' r='4'/></g>

karty.g: Players communicate as people do in the game world, without leaving their roles.
karty.nz: The game must give players a reason and a way to speak in character, and avoid options that pull them out of it. Separate channels for out-of-game talk help.
karty.yr: A fantasy setting where players chat about scores and tactics in ordinary terms the whole time.
karty.rk: which channels exist; how strongly in-character talk is encouraged

karty.g: Nothing appears on screen that doesn't exist in the game world itself.
karty.nz: Everything shown must belong to the game world, so interface elements, scores and hints must be kept out or disguised as part of it. Repeated actions such as retries must also make sense in the world.
karty.yr: A world that looks real but shows floating score counters and tooltips all over the screen.
karty.rk: how much non-world interface is shown; how it is styled
karty.ik: <rect x='6' y='6' width='52' height='52' rx='4'/><circle cx='44' cy='24' r='6' fill='#c9a24a'/><path d='M6 56l16-20 12 14 8-8 16 14' fill='#4fa83a'/><rect x='12' y='12' width='20' height='6' rx='2' stroke='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3' stroke-dasharray='3 4'/>

karty.g: Parts of the world stand out by shape, color, or texture and hint at what can be done with them.
karty.nz: The feature must stand out from its surroundings and mean something consistent, so that players learn what it signals. It should still fit the world.
karty.yr: Something is shiny or colored differently but the look has no link to what it is or does.
karty.rk: how strongly it stands out; how reliably it signals the same thing
karty.ik: <path d='M32 58V34'/><circle cx='32' cy='22' r='16' fill='#c9a24a'/><path d='M2 58c0-9 12-9 12 0z' fill='#d5d9e0' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M50 58c0-9 12-9 12 0z' fill='#d5d9e0' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M2 60h60'/>

karty.g: Items that really exist inside the game world, which can be seen and picked up.
karty.nz: The items must take part in the game's physics or rules, blocking movement or sight or being moved and broken. Players must be able to interact with them.
karty.yr: Objects that are drawn solid but can be walked through and do nothing.
karty.rk: which items are solid; whether they can be moved or destroyed

karty.g: A setting where the player chooses how hard the game will be.
karty.nz: Each level must change the play in a meaningful way, such as the enemies' numbers, skill or the player's resources. Players must be able to pick and change the level.
karty.yr: A menu with easy, normal and hard that only change a name or a small number, so the games feel the same.
karty.rk: what each level changes; how many levels; whether the level can be changed during play
karty.ik: <path d='M8 44A24 24 0 0 1 20 23.2' stroke='#4fa83a' stroke-width='6'/><path d='M20 23.2A24 24 0 0 1 44 23.2' stroke='#c9a24a' stroke-width='6'/><path d='M44 23.2A24 24 0 0 1 56 44' stroke='#e85d4f' stroke-width='6'/><path d='M32 44L44 28'/><circle cx='32' cy='44' r='5' fill='#2a2a2a'/><path d='M10 58h44'/>

karty.g: A place where cards or tiles are put after they have been played.
karty.nz: The pile must have a rule for whether it is open or closed and whether cards come back. Its contents must matter, for example by refilling the deck or being searchable.
karty.yr: A pile where used cards just sit, nobody looks at it and it never affects play.
karty.rk: open or closed; whether cards can be retrieved; whether it refills the deck
karty.ik: <rect x='8' y='32' width='24' height='28' rx='3' fill='#fff' transform='rotate(-12 20 46)'/><rect x='30' y='34' width='24' height='26' rx='3' fill='#fff' transform='rotate(10 42 47)'/><rect x='17' y='30' width='24' height='28' rx='3' fill='#d5d9e0'/><path d='M32 4v12' stroke='#e85d4f'/><polyline points='26 11 32 17 38 11' stroke='#e85d4f'/>

karty.g: Time when a player has to wait during a game session.
karty.nz: It comes from rules that block actions, such as turn order, penalties or slow players. It stays bearable when there is something to watch or plan.
karty.yr: A pause screen of a second or two that nobody notices as waiting.
karty.rk: length of enforced waits; how often they occur; what players can do during them
karty.ik: <circle cx='28' cy='32' r='18' fill='#c9a24a'/><circle cx='28' cy='32' r='8'/><path d='M8 56h42c8 0 10-8 8-18' fill='none'/><path d='M55 40l-3-12M60 42l3-10' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: Players take turns choosing game elements from a shared set until the choices run out.
karty.nz: There must be real choices between elements of differing value, with a clear order of picking. The picks must carry on to later play.
karty.yr: Players take items one at a time but they are all the same or the choice is forced, so it is only a handout.
karty.rk: how many options per pick; order of picking; how many picks
karty.ik: <rect x='4' y='26' width='22' height='30' rx='3' fill='#fff'/><rect x='8' y='22' width='22' height='30' rx='3' fill='#fff'/><rect x='36' y='6' width='22' height='30' rx='3' fill='#c9a24a' transform='rotate(10 47 21)'/><path d='M34 52h22' stroke='#e85d4f'/><polyline points='50 46 56 52 50 58' stroke='#e85d4f'/>

karty.g: The options players take turns choosing from are laid out in view of everyone.
karty.nz: The display must show several different elements that are refilled in a clear way. Their values must differ so that choosing and watching others matters.
karty.yr: A display where all cards are alike or the order is fixed, so picking is not a decision.
karty.rk: number of cards shown; how it is refilled; extra cost to pick deeper ones
karty.ik: <rect x='4' y='14' width='16' height='32' rx='3' fill='#fff'/><rect x='24' y='14' width='16' height='32' rx='3' fill='#c9a24a'/><rect x='44' y='14' width='16' height='32' rx='3' fill='#fff'/><circle cx='12' cy='30' r='2' fill='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/><circle cx='32' cy='30' r='2' fill='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/><circle cx='52' cy='30' r='2' fill='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M4 56h56'/>

karty.g: A stack of cards or tiles in a set order, drawn from to determine an outcome.
karty.nz: The pile must be hidden and shuffled, and its mix of element types must be set on purpose so the odds are real. Players need reasons to care what comes next, such as hands to build or plans to make.
karty.yr: A pile of cards that is never shuffled or whose contents are all the same, so what comes out is known and drawing changes no decision.
karty.rk: what goes into the stack and in what mix; number of stacks; how it is seeded or shuffled
karty.ik: <rect x='6' y='10' width='26' height='36' rx='3' fill='#fff'/><rect x='10' y='14' width='26' height='36' rx='3' fill='#fff'/><rect x='14' y='18' width='26' height='36' rx='3' fill='#2f6b8f'/><path d='M27 28l6 8-6 8-6-8z' fill='#c9a24a' stroke-width='2'/><rect x='38' y='24' width='20' height='28' rx='3' fill='#fff' transform='rotate(12 48 38)'/>

karty.g: The game is built so players can join and leave during a session.
karty.nz: The game must keep working when the player count changes: it needs a way to rebalance, hand over or park a leaver's pieces, and bring a returner back without wasting others' effort.
karty.yr: A menu that says you may join or leave at any time, yet a leaver breaks the game or a newcomer is hopelessly behind and cannot take part.
karty.rk: how and when players may join or leave; what happens to their assets; how newcomers are caught up or balanced
karty.ik: <rect x='32' y='8' width='26' height='50' rx='2' fill='#d5d9e0'/><path d='M4 22h22' stroke='#4fa83a' stroke-width='5'/><polyline points='20 16 26 22 20 28' stroke='#4fa83a' stroke-width='5'/><path d='M28 44H6' stroke='#e85d4f' stroke-width='5'/><polyline points='12 38 6 44 12 50' stroke='#e85d4f' stroke-width='5'/>

karty.g: The game changes its difficulty by itself depending on how the player is doing.
karty.nz: The game must measure performance reliably and link it to parameters that really change the challenge, with changes gentle enough not to feel like cheating or to be easily gamed.
karty.yr: A system that is switched on but whose adjustments are so small, or tied to a poor measure, that a good and a bad player face the same challenge.
karty.rk: what performance is measured; how strongly and how quickly difficulty reacts; whether it is visible or optional
karty.ik: <path d='M6 6v52h52'/><path d='M12 32h46' stroke='#c9a24a' stroke-dasharray='4 5'/><path d='M12 48c8-24 14 4 22-14s12 6 24-18' stroke='#e85d4f'/>

karty.g: Goal: the conditions of the goal itself change as the game goes on.
karty.nz: Changes must follow clear rules and be visible enough that players can replan, yet not so large that the goal feels like a different one.
karty.yr: A goal whose displayed numbers or wording shift but whose real task, cost and approach stay the same.
karty.rk: which goal parameter changes; how big and how frequent the changes are; what triggers them
karty.ik: <circle cx='40' cy='32' r='18' fill='#fff'/><circle cx='40' cy='32' r='9' fill='#e85d4f'/><path d='M4 20h10M4 32h6M4 44h10' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: A player is knocked out long before the session ends for everyone else.
karty.nz: Players must be able to lose out long before the game ends, and no role is kept for them, so they wait a long time. The effect grows with game length and a lack of short rounds.
karty.yr: An elimination rule that exists but only triggers in the last minutes, so nobody sits out for long.
karty.rk: how easy and how early elimination is; game length; what eliminated players can still do
karty.ik: <g transform='rotate(80 32 34)'><circle cx='32' cy='14' r='8' fill='#e85d4f'/><path d='M24 52c0-14 4-18 8-22 4 4 8 8 8 22z' fill='#e85d4f'/><path d='M18 54h28'/></g><path d='M4 58h56' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: Players abandon the session before the end, though the game didn't force them to.
karty.nz: Leaving becomes likely when games run long, feel lost or depend heavily on others; the design must decide how the game copes when someone departs.
karty.yr: A rule saying what happens when someone leaves, in a game short or engaging enough that nobody ever does.
karty.rk: game length; how hopeless a losing position feels; what the game does with a departed player's position
karty.ik: <path d='M18 6v30h26M18 36v22M44 36v22'/><rect x='16' y='34' width='30' height='7' rx='2' fill='#c9a24a' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M4 58h56' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: Hidden surprises unrelated to the game's story and world.
karty.nz: The secret must be hidden well enough to feel like a discovery but findable through exploration or hints, and it must be fun or funny when found. Players also need a reason to suspect secrets exist.
karty.yr: A hidden thing that is trivially visible, or so obscure and dull that nobody finds it or cares when they do.
karty.rk: how many there are; how hidden they are; how strongly clues point to them

karty.g: Goal: remove certain elements from the game.
karty.nz: There must be targets that can be removed and ways for players to remove them, and the goal must matter to winning or progress so players pursue it.
karty.yr: Targets that are listed as removable but cannot be hurt in practice, or removing them gains nothing.
karty.rk: how many targets; how hard they are to remove; what removal gives

karty.g: Commands with which a player shows their hero's feelings without affecting the game's course.
karty.nz: Players need a simple way to trigger the actions, visible to nearby others, and a reason to use them such as social play or role-playing.
karty.yr: A few emote buttons that nobody sees, or whose output is the same canned animation that carries no personal expression.
karty.rk: freeform or fixed list; how many emotes; who sees them and how they are labelled
karty.ik: <circle cx='32' cy='32' r='26' fill='#c9a24a'/><path d='M23 24h0M41 24h0' stroke-width='6'/><path d='M18 38c6 12 22 12 28 0' stroke-width='4'/>

karty.g: Game characters show noticeable feelings toward phenomena and creatures of the game world.
karty.nz: Characters need reactions that fit events and relationships and visible consequences of what happens to them, so players believe they care.
karty.yr: A character who says it is sad or fond in a line of text but acts exactly the same afterwards.
karty.rk: how many events characters react to; strength and visibility of reactions; how long memory of events lasts
karty.ik: <circle cx='13' cy='15' r='8' fill='#c9a24a'/><circle cx='51' cy='15' r='8' fill='#c9a24a'/><circle cx='32' cy='34' r='20' fill='#c9a24a'/><ellipse cx='32' cy='42' rx='9' ry='7' fill='#fff'/><path d='M24 30h0M40 30h0' stroke-width='5'/><circle cx='32' cy='40' r='2.5' fill='#e85d4f' stroke='none'/>

karty.g: The player personally does and says what their character does and says.
karty.nz: The game needs characters, a setting that invites in-character action and an audience of other players; rules should reward or at least allow performance.
karty.yr: Players pick a character name and class but speak and act as themselves.
karty.rk: how much the rules reward in-character play; presence of a facilitator or audience; warm-up support

karty.g: Goal: surround game elements with an unbroken line or wall made of other elements.
karty.nz: Pieces need placement or movement rules that allow forming a closed boundary, and enclosing must earn something such as capture or ownership.
karty.yr: An enclosing shape that can be formed but gives no benefit, or the board makes closing it impossible.
karty.rk: size of the board; what can enclose and be enclosed; what enclosing yields
karty.ik: <circle cx='14' cy='14' r='5' fill='#2f6b8f'/><circle cx='32' cy='14' r='5' fill='#2f6b8f'/><circle cx='50' cy='14' r='5' fill='#2f6b8f'/><circle cx='14' cy='32' r='5' fill='#2f6b8f'/><circle cx='50' cy='32' r='5' fill='#2f6b8f'/><circle cx='14' cy='50' r='5' fill='#2f6b8f'/><circle cx='32' cy='50' r='5' fill='#2f6b8f'/><circle cx='50' cy='50' r='5' fill='#2f6b8f'/><circle cx='32' cy='32' r='6' fill='#e85d4f'/>

karty.g: Game design that makes players want to come back to the same places and activities.
karty.nz: The game must be persistent and able to be left and re-entered, with timers, regenerating resources or growing rewards that make coming back worthwhile.
karty.yr: A daily login prompt or reminder with a trivial reward that players claim and ignore.
karty.rk: length of timers; regeneration rate; size and growth of rewards for repeated visits
karty.ik: <path d='M14 40L32 26l18 14v18H14z' fill='#c9a24a'/><path d='M28 58V46h8v12'/><path d='M8 30a26 26 0 0 1 48 0' stroke='#e85d4f'/><path d='M57 21l-1 10-9-4' stroke='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: Points are added up only after the game has ended.
karty.nz: A large share of points must be hidden or uncounted until the end and depend on the final state, so players cannot easily calculate standings.
karty.yr: A final tally that merely repeats a score everyone already knows, so the end changes nothing.
karty.rk: how many points are held until the end; how hidden the scoring is; what final conditions give points
karty.ik: <rect x='6' y='10' width='52' height='44' rx='3'/><path d='M6 32h52'/><circle cx='18' cy='21' r='5' fill='#c9a24a'/><circle cx='30' cy='21' r='5' fill='#c9a24a'/><circle cx='44' cy='43' r='5' fill='#c9a24a'/><circle cx='32' cy='43' r='5' fill='#c9a24a'/><circle cx='20' cy='43' r='5' fill='#c9a24a'/>

karty.g: A final stage that happens in every play of this game.
karty.nz: Earlier play must lead to a state with a distinct character, such as fewer options, high stakes or elimination, and the game needs a regular way of finishing.
karty.yr: A phase labelled endgame in the rules that plays like the middle game, with the game just stopping.
karty.rk: what ends the game; how play narrows toward the end; how strongly earlier choices matter at the end

karty.g: Goal: complete a task available only at the end of the game, with a reward suited to that stage.
karty.nz: Quests must be unlocked by reaching the end phase and be hard enough for experienced characters, with rewards that matter to players who have already maxed out.
karty.yr: Extra quests that are just earlier quests with bigger numbers, giving rewards nobody needs.
karty.rk: unlock condition; difficulty; reward type and value

karty.g: Game elements that actively get in the way of the player reaching their goals.
karty.nz: Enemies must act against the player's goals with real consequences, and the player needs ways to face them; they also need to fit the theme to be recognised.
karty.yr: Enemies drawn as threatening but too weak or passive to hurt or block anyone.
karty.rk: number of enemies; their strength and behaviour; how they appear

karty.g: A punishment that reduces a numeric supply the player needs to take actions.
karty.nz: The value must matter for actions and lead to a worse outcome at some threshold; the loss must be large enough to notice and be recoverable or not by design.
karty.yr: A health bar that drops but regenerates instantly or never reaches a threshold, so nothing is at risk.
karty.rk: amount lost per event; starting amount and maximum; recovery rate and threshold effects
karty.ik: <rect x='6' y='18' width='46' height='28' rx='4'/><path d='M52 27h6v10h-6'/><rect x='11' y='23' width='9' height='18' rx='1' fill='#e85d4f' stroke='none'/><path d='M32 52v8M26 56l6 6 6-6' stroke='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3' />

karty.g: A character is forced to take certain actions so that their personality is kept or developed.
karty.nz: The game must actually limit available actions or take control at set points, and the enforced behaviour must fit the character or story.
karty.yr: A character described as loyal or cowardly whom the player can still make do anything.
karty.rk: which actions are forbidden or forced; when control is taken; how strictly this applies
karty.ik: <path d='M16 6h32'/><path d='M20 6v28M44 6v28M32 6v14' stroke-width='2.5'/><circle cx='32' cy='26' r='6' fill='#c9a24a'/><path d='M23 58l3-20h12l3 20z' fill='#2f6b8f'/>

karty.g: The system itself hides from players who the other players are.
karty.nz: The game must remove or limit names, friend lists and open chat, so players really cannot tell who others are or contact them outside gameplay.
karty.yr: Anonymous-looking nicknames that are still consistent and linkable, and open chat that lets players reveal who they are.
karty.rk: what identity info is hidden; which communication channels exist; whether exceptions for known friends are allowed
karty.ik: <circle cx='32' cy='32' r='24'/><path d='M8 26h48v12H8z' fill='#2a2a2a'/><circle cx='22' cy='32' r='3' fill='#fff' stroke='none'/><circle cx='42' cy='32' r='3' fill='#fff' stroke='none'/>

karty.g: Players get the right to change how the game goes and are responsible for everyone's experience.
karty.nz: Some players must get real powers over how the game runs, such as creating content or removing players, along with a role that expects them to use these for others' benefit.
karty.yr: A title or badge for certain players that gives them no abilities to shape the game.
karty.rk: which powers are granted; who gets the role; limits on how powers are used
karty.ik: <path d='M6 14h52M6 32h52M6 50h52'/><circle cx='18' cy='14' r='6' fill='#c9a24a'/><circle cx='42' cy='32' r='6' fill='#e85d4f'/><circle cx='28' cy='50' r='6' fill='#2f6b8f'/>

karty.g: As the game goes on, the situation becomes harder and harder to change.
karty.nz: Actions must be irreversible and combine so that earlier choices lock in later ones; resource loss helps. Reversibility must be mostly avoided.
karty.yr: Irreversible-looking moves that are easy to undo or have so little effect that the state remains open to the end.
karty.rk: how irreversible actions are; how strongly effects accumulate; resource depletion rate
karty.ik: <path d='M4 24h14v26h28V24h14'/><ellipse cx='11' cy='19' rx='8' ry='4' fill='#c9a24a'/><ellipse cx='53' cy='19' rx='8' ry='4' fill='#c9a24a'/><path d='M4 58h56'/>

karty.g: In a certain part of the world, actions and events work differently than elsewhere.
karty.nz: Each area needs a rule that alters actions, movement or events, and it should be noticeable and matter to choices of where to go.
karty.yr: Areas with a different look or label that behave exactly like all others.
karty.rk: which areas have effects; effect type and strength; whether permanent or temporary

karty.g: The story is revealed as the player walks around and explores a place.
karty.nz: The world must hold readable traces of past events in props, items and layout, placed where players pass, and players need freedom and a reason to look and interpret.
karty.yr: Decor that is only decor, or story info tucked in a place nobody sees and tells them nothing about what happened.
karty.rk: density and placement of story clues; how obvious they are; how much is optional

karty.g: Events that exist in the game only for a limited time and then disappear.
karty.nz: Events must start and end by clear rules, last briefly in game time, and offer something that is not available otherwise.
karty.yr: An event that is announced as limited but lasts so long or repeats so often that missing it costs nothing.
karty.rk: duration; frequency; what triggers them; what they offer
karty.ik: <circle cx='44' cy='20' r='10' fill='#c9a24a'/><path d='M36 28L8 56M32 20L12 40M44 32L24 52' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: Goal: it appears and disappears mid-game, and you can fail it through no fault of your own.
karty.nz: Goals must appear and expire during play on their own terms, with failure possible beyond the player's actions, and be worth chasing.
karty.yr: Temporary goals that stay available long enough that everyone completes them eventually, so timing never matters.
karty.rk: how often goals appear; how long they last; how they are triggered, random or state-based
karty.ik: <circle cx='32' cy='32' r='25' stroke-dasharray='3 7'/><path d='M24 46V16' /><path d='M24 16l18 6-18 8z' fill='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: Items that a character can wear or hold in their hands.
karty.nz: Items must change what the character can do when equipped, and there must be several to choose from with trade-offs, so choosing matters.
karty.yr: Items that can be equipped but give only cosmetic changes or are strictly better than every alternative.
karty.rk: number of equippable items; strength of their bonuses; wear or limited uses

karty.g: Spaces where the player puts the items they want to use.
karty.nz: Slots must be limited and specialised so that choosing for one means giving up another, and items must differ enough to make that a real trade-off.
karty.yr: Slots that can always be filled with the same best items so there is never a choice.
karty.rk: number and types of slots; whether they replace or add to an inventory; how much items differ

karty.g: Goal: avoid being caught and avoid being hit.
karty.nz: There must be a clear threat with a penalty if it hits, and the player must have means of avoiding it, such as movement, and a real chance of failing.
karty.yr: A danger so slow or easy to dodge that it can be ignored, or a hit that costs nothing.
karty.rk: speed and accuracy of threats; the player's mobility; penalty for being hit
karty.ik: <path d='M4 18h38' stroke='#e85d4f'/><path d='M54 18l-12-7v14z' fill='#e85d4f'/><circle cx='20' cy='42' r='6'/><path d='M12 60l4-12h12l4 12z' fill='#2f6b8f'/><path d='M44 40l10 6' stroke-dasharray='1 7'/>

karty.n: Events Timed to the Real World
karty.g: Game events are triggered when a certain moment in real time arrives.
karty.nz: The game must run in real time or ticks and know the real date or time, and the event must offer something worth showing up for, with players told in advance.
karty.yr: A holiday theme that is only a visual reskin with no different gameplay or rewards, so nobody schedules around it.
karty.rk: which real-world dates trigger events; event length; how far ahead players are told
karty.ik: <rect x='8' y='10' width='48' height='46' rx='4'/><path d='M8 22h48M20 5v10M44 5v10'/><circle cx='38' cy='40' r='7' fill='#e85d4f'/>

karty.g: The more successfully the player plays, the harder the challenges become.
karty.nz: Success must feed back into a harder next challenge, such as stronger enemies, bigger waves or tougher levels, and the climb must be steady and outpace most players' skill. Without an end condition, or with one far away, the difficulty keeps rising instead of flattening.
karty.yr: Enemies get bigger numbers or new skins, but skilled players still cruise through because nothing demands more skill.
karty.rk: difficulty growth rate per success; step size and ceiling of the scaling curve
karty.ik: <path d='M4 58V46h14V34h14V22h14V8h14v50z' fill='#e85d4f'/>

karty.g: New rules are added to the game as it goes on.
karty.nz: There has to be a channel to deliver new rules (patches, expansions, a game master, legacy-style carry-over) and the rule set must be large enough that changes alter what good play is. Players need to be told or able to find out what changed.
karty.yr: A patch that only fixes bugs or adds cosmetic items, so the way anyone plays stays exactly the same.
karty.rk: how often rules change; how big each change is and what it touches (new abilities, removals, balance)
karty.ik: <rect x='6' y='6' width='36' height='52' rx='3'/><path d='M13 18h22M13 28h22M13 38h12' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M50 28v20M40 38h20' stroke='#4fa83a' stroke-width='5'/>

karty.g: The player feels they affect the outcome, whether or not they really do.
karty.nz: Give players many visible options and strong-feeling feedback for their actions, such as buffs, tools and abilities, while keeping the real outcome only loosely tied to them. It has to stay hidden: if players figure out the trick, or fully master the game, the feeling collapses.
karty.yr: A flashy upgrade or button that plainly does nothing, which players spot quickly and then feel cheated rather than powerful.
karty.rk: how strong and how numerous the visible player controls are, compared with their real effect on the outcome
karty.ik: <path d='M20 58V36'/><circle cx='20' cy='30' r='6' fill='#c9a24a'/><path d='M8 56h24'/><path d='M30 12a28 28 0 0 1 28 28' stroke='#e85d4f' stroke-dasharray='1 7'/><path d='M58 40l-8-6M58 40l2-10' stroke='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: Rare events that are remembered because they are so unlikely or affect the game so strongly.
karty.nz: Include rare, high-impact or surprising outcomes (critical results, betrayals, spectacular failures) that cannot be undone at once. Hidden information and randomness help, but the events must really change the game state, not just flash by.
karty.yr: A rare-sounding event that happens often, or one that changes nothing and is quickly reversed, so nobody remembers it.
karty.rk: how rare the event is; how large and how permanent its effect on the game state

karty.g: Side actions that are required to play but add nothing to the game by themselves.
karty.nz: It appears when the game state must be updated by hand (bookkeeping, tracking statistics, handling many units or characters) with nobody or nothing doing it automatically. To avoid it, automate the upkeep or fold it into real choices.
karty.yr: A task that merely looks like chores, such as a quick, enjoyable action that is actually a meaningful choice, so it is not true excise.
karty.rk: how much state players must maintain by hand; how much of it is automated
karty.ik: <path d='M50 4L30 36'/><path d='M22 34l14 8 6 14H12c0-8 4-18 10-22z' fill='#c9a24a'/><path d='M18 48l6-6M26 50l4-6' stroke-width='2.500'/><path d='M44 56h0M54 52h0M50 60h0' stroke-width='4' stroke='#d5d9e0'/>

karty.g: Goal: choose one of several, because completing one closes off the others.
karty.nz: Define goals whose completion conditions really conflict, with clear rules for who or what wins when they clash (usually order of completion or a tiebreaker). Players need to be able to choose among them for the trade-off to matter.
karty.yr: Several goals are listed as alternatives, but a player can achieve all of them anyway, so nothing is given up.
karty.rk: how many goals exclude each other; whether exclusion is between players or within one player's own choices

karty.g: A stage where the main aim is to increase the share of the game world you control.
karty.nz: The game needs a world big enough to grow into, a way to own territory (occupation or building), and costs or unlocks that pace how fast growth happens. Goals that reward gaining ownership push players into it.
karty.yr: A map with claimable spots, but claiming gives no benefit or is capped so tightly that nobody spends a phase of play on growing.
karty.rk: map size and terrain; cost and unlock requirements for claiming or building
karty.ik: <rect x='6' y='6' width='52' height='52' rx='2' stroke-dasharray='1 7'/><rect x='6' y='24' width='34' height='34' fill='#c9a24a' fill-opacity='.45'/><rect x='6' y='42' width='16' height='16' fill='#c9a24a'/><path d='M30 34l22-22M52 12H40M52 12v12' stroke='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: Trial actions to learn the rules and game state or to practice skills.
karty.nz: Failure must be cheap and actions reversible, and the game must have something worth finding out (hidden information, complex systems, enemy weaknesses) with predictable cause and effect. Heavy penalties or too much randomness make players stop trying things.
karty.yr: A sandbox with lots of options, but one mistake is punished harshly or results are so random that nothing can be learned.
karty.rk: cost of failure and reversibility of actions; how much randomness hides cause and effect

karty.g: The player can enter the number from which the game builds its randomness.
karty.nz: The game must have a seeded random generator and show a clear way for players to enter and share the seed. The same seed then has to give the same results every time.
karty.yr: A seed field exists, but the game mixes in the clock or other randomness, so identical seeds give different worlds.
karty.rk: what the seed controls (whole world, level layout, just a setup); how visible the seed input is
karty.ik: <rect x='6' y='26' width='32' height='32' rx='5' fill='#fff'/><circle cx='16' cy='36' r='2.500' fill='#2a2a2a' stroke='none'/><circle cx='22' cy='42' r='2.500' fill='#2a2a2a' stroke='none'/><circle cx='28' cy='48' r='2.500' fill='#2a2a2a' stroke='none'/><ellipse cx='48' cy='28' rx='5' ry='7' fill='#c9a24a'/><path d='M48 21c0-8 4-12 10-14' stroke='#4fa83a'/>

karty.g: A game stage where the main aim is to use what you already have as efficiently as possible.
karty.nz: Players need owned resources, locations and abilities to optimize, plus enough system depth that efficient setups (gameplay engines) beat sloppy ones. Unlock timing and costs decide when this stage starts.
karty.yr: Resources are available, but there is only one obvious best use, so there is nothing to optimize and no phase of optimizing.
karty.rk: resource yield and number of resource sources; when optimizing abilities become available
karty.ik: <circle cx='32' cy='32' r='18' stroke-width='7' stroke-dasharray='6 8.100'/><circle cx='32' cy='32' r='14' fill='#c9a24a'/><circle cx='32' cy='32' r='5' fill='#fff'/>

karty.g: An action lasts so long that nothing else can be done during that time.
karty.nz: The action must take long enough that doing it means giving up other actions, and it should carry risk, such as being interruptible or locking the player in. Effects can scale with duration or kick in after a threshold.
karty.yr: A short animation or brief delay that never stops the player from doing anything else, so no real trade-off exists.
karty.rk: duration required; whether it can be interrupted and how effects scale with time
karty.ik: <path d='M18 6c26 10 26 42 0 52'/><path d='M18 6L40 32L18 58' stroke-width='2.500'/><path d='M40 32h16' /><path d='M60 32l-8-5v10z' fill='#e85d4f' stroke-width='2'/>

karty.g: A stage of play where the main task is to destroy, most often other players.
karty.nz: Elimination goals and combat must be available, with the strongest combat units or tools held back until late. Games must be long enough to contain distinct phases, and elimination must really be possible.
karty.yr: Attacking is allowed from turn one and nobody can be eliminated, so no distinct late stage of destruction ever forms.
karty.rk: when strong combat units unlock; whether and how players can be eliminated

karty.g: You can try again if you are not happy with the result of an action.
karty.nz: Decide which events can be retried, how many retries exist, how they are earned or refilled, and whether retries can be stacked. The game state must allow trying again, and other players' actions must not make the retry impossible.
karty.yr: A retry that is so limited, or so late, that players never actually use it to change an outcome.
karty.rk: how many retries; how they are gained and which events they apply to

karty.g: A player takes another turn right after their own turn.
karty.nz: Specify the trigger (a reward, a roll, a card) and whether the player controls when it happens. Because it can double a player's actions, it must be balanced against how strong a single turn is.
karty.yr: An 'extra turn' that has nothing meaningful left to do, or comes only when the game is already decided.
karty.rk: how often extra turns are granted; what triggers them and whether players choose when
karty.ik: <circle cx='24' cy='16' r='8'/><path d='M12 52h24l-5-24H17z' fill='#2f6b8f'/><path d='M44 22c10 0 14 12 8 20s-14 6-14 6' stroke='#e85d4f'/><path d='M40 54l-3-6 7-3' stroke='#e85d4f' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: Acts prompted by the game that do not affect the current play.
karty.nz: The game needs real value in preparing, documenting, negotiating or running things outside the game state, such as planning, saving, storytelling or creating content, and the rules or interface must support it. Players should gain something from them later.
karty.yr: A menu or notebook option that nobody has a reason to use because nothing in play benefits from it.
karty.rk: how much the game supports and rewards out-of-game preparation, sharing or record keeping
karty.ik: <rect x='8' y='8' width='34' height='48' rx='3'/><path d='M16 22h18M16 32h18M16 42h10' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M50 8l8 8-18 24-9 2 2-9z' fill='#c9a24a'/>

karty.g: Game events are sent out through channels other than the one where the game is played.
karty.nz: Decide which events get sent, when and through what channel, and put players in control of sharing so it does not feel like spam. Events like achievements, rewards and uncertain moments are worth sending.
karty.yr: A share button or notification stream that sends trivial events nobody wants to see, so no one outside the game ever reacts.
karty.rk: which events are broadcast; how often and through which channel

karty.g: Events in the game affect something outside it, for better or worse.
karty.nz: The game's results must really feed into something outside the game state, such as prizes, money, the next game session's rules or another game. Players must know about the link and care about it.
karty.yr: A 'real-world prize' or carry-over that players find worthless or that never actually changes anything outside the match.
karty.rk: what outside thing results are tied to (money, rewards, future games); how large the stakes are

karty.g: The game's state changes something outside it, and neither a player nor the rules does so.
karty.nz: Pick the outside source (real-world time, other games, non-players, facilitators), and give the game rules for accepting and processing that input. Players must be able to see how the source affects play.
karty.yr: A feature that reads an outside signal but never lets it change anything meaningful in the game state.
karty.rk: which outside sources are allowed; how strongly their input alters the game state
karty.ik: <path d='M24 4v14M40 4v14'/><rect x='14' y='18' width='36' height='20' rx='6' fill='#2f6b8f'/><path d='M32 38v8c0 10 14 6 14 16' /><path d='M54 40l-8 8h8l-6 8' stroke='#c9a24a' stroke-width='3'/>

karty.g: Rewards that make later actions or progress through the game easier.
karty.nz: The reward must actually change what players can do or how easily they do it, such as new abilities, better tools, stronger skills or progress toward the end. The strength should match the effort required to earn it.
karty.yr: A reward that looks like a power-up but gives a negligible bonus, so play is no easier than before.
karty.rk: size of the ability or power boost; how often and how hard it is to earn

karty.g: Groups in the game world united by which deeds they reward and forbid.
karty.nz: Set clear criteria to join, stay and advance, and make group membership change what members can do or must do. Gatekeepers, quests or requirements make joining meaningful, and group rules must be enforced.
karty.yr: A faction label or banner that has no effect on abilities, access, goals or how others treat the player.
karty.rk: requirements to join and stay; how many factions one can belong to and what membership grants
karty.ik: <path d='M6 8h52'/><path d='M14 8v34l18 14 18-14V8z' fill='#e85d4f'/><circle cx='32' cy='24' r='7' fill='#c9a24a'/>

karty.g: The game pretends to be shut down so it can later surprise players with a continuation.
karty.nz: The game needs a believable cancellation message through some channel, and contact details collected beforehand so players can be reached again. It only fits games meant to blur the line between game and real life.
karty.yr: A cancellation notice so unconvincing, or with no way to contact players again, that nobody is surprised or it simply ends the game.
karty.rk: how convincing and through which channel the cancellation is announced; how long before players are re-contacted
karty.ik: <rect x="8" y="14" width="48" height="36" rx="4" fill="#fff"/><path d="M16 42L48 22" stroke="#e85d4f" stroke-width="5"/><path d="M20 56h24"/><path d="M44 8c4 0 8 3 8 8" stroke-width="3"/><circle cx="32" cy="32" r="5" fill="#c9a24a"/>

karty.g: The game announces that everything is over when in fact it is not.
karty.nz: The game needs a believable game over presentation, then a clear resumption of play. It fits only games where a real game over exists and carries weight, so the fake can shock players.
karty.yr: A game over screen that is obviously fake or comes with no loss, so players feel no sense of failure.
karty.rk: how convincing the fake ending is; how and when play resumes
karty.ik: <rect x="6" y="10" width="52" height="36" rx="4"/><path d="M20 56h24M32 46v10"/><path d="M20 20l10 16M30 20L20 36" stroke="#e85d4f" stroke-width="5"/><path d="M38 36l5-8 5 8" stroke="#4fa83a" stroke-width="4"/>

karty.g: Real physical items packaged with the game that strengthen the impression it makes.
karty.nz: Props must fit the game's world and tone and ideally carry clues, backstory or help, so that using them deepens immersion. They must be made to match the theme of the game.
karty.yr: Generic box extras, such as stickers or a poster, with no link to the story or play, so they add nothing to the experience.
karty.rk: how many props; how themed they are and whether they carry clues or helpful information

karty.g: The game master rolls dice for show, and the result does not affect how the game goes.
karty.nz: Needs a human game master, hidden rolls, and players who cannot check results (screens, secret rolls). The game master must be willing to override outcomes to shape the story.
karty.yr: The game master rolls openly in front of everyone or follows the dice anyway, so the roll is not feigned at all.
karty.rk: how many rolls are hidden; how often the game master ignores or overrides the dice
karty.ik: <rect x="14" y="22" width="36" height="36" rx="6" fill="#fff"/><circle cx="24" cy="32" r="2.5" fill="#2a2a2a"/><circle cx="40" cy="48" r="2.5" fill="#2a2a2a"/><circle cx="32" cy="40" r="2.5" fill="#2a2a2a"/><path d="M4 14c8-6 16-6 24 0" stroke-width="3"/><path d="M8 8l20 8" stroke="#e85d4f" stroke-width="3"/>

karty.g: Levels built to feel like the conclusion of a storyline.
karty.nz: Build the last area to resolve the narrative arc, with harder play and a boss or climax, positioned so it feels like the end. The difficulty and story should peak together.
karty.yr: The last level is just another ordinary level with a credits screen, with no rise in challenge or sense of closure.
karty.rk: difficulty spike of the final level; how much story resolution it carries

karty.g: The benefit of taking actions before everyone else.
karty.nz: Needs turn-based play where moving first matters and starting positions are equal. The size of the edge depends on how much a single move can change the game, and balancing needs its own fix such as rotating order.
karty.yr: Players are labelled first, but moving first changes nothing, so no advantage exists.
karty.rk: how much one early move is worth; whether compensation (turn rotation, bonuses for later players) is added
karty.ik: <path d="M4 54h56"/><path d="M10 54V44h14v10M24 54V34h14v20" fill="#d5d9e0"/><path d="M38 54V24h14v30" fill="#c9a24a"/><path d="M45 22V8"/><circle cx="45" cy="8" r="3" fill="#e85d4f"/>

karty.g: A token shows who goes first in the turn order.
karty.nz: The game must have a changing turn order across rounds and the token must be passed according to clear rules. For orders with more than two positions, more markers or an order track may be needed.
karty.yr: A token that stays with one player or is ignored because the order never changes.
karty.rk: how the token is passed; how many positions in the order need markers

karty.g: The world is shown as a creature inside that world would see it.
karty.nz: Needs an avatar in the game world and a camera or presentation that shows only what that avatar could perceive, including line of sight. For immersion, movement and aiming should respond naturally.
karty.yr: A camera placed at the character's head height that still shows the player things the avatar could not perceive, such as through walls.
karty.rk: field of view and what the avatar can see; whether players can switch viewpoints

karty.g: Guaranteed randomness: by known moments, a preset set of outcomes will have come up.
karty.nz: The game must draw from a limited pool without replacement (like a deck) or force a spread over a cycle, and let players know or track what has appeared. Visible history lets them predict what is left.
karty.yr: A shuffled deck that is reshuffled every draw or a random roll, so past results never constrain future ones.
karty.rk: cycle length or pool size; whether players can see what has already been drawn
karty.ik: <rect x="6" y="10" width="20" height="20" rx="4" fill="#fff"/><circle cx="16" cy="20" r="2.5" fill="#2a2a2a"/><rect x="38" y="10" width="20" height="20" rx="4" fill="#fff"/><circle cx="44" cy="16" r="2.5" fill="#2a2a2a"/><circle cx="52" cy="24" r="2.5" fill="#2a2a2a"/><path d="M6 42h14v14H6zM25 42h14v14H25zM44 42h14v14H44z" fill="#4fa83a" stroke-width="3"/>

karty.g: Alternative paths to the needed place that others may not know about.
karty.nz: Add alternative paths to key locations that are less obvious or less defended than the main route. For them to matter, defenders must be unable to guard everything and the routes must lead to something worth reaching.
karty.yr: Extra paths that are as obvious as the main route or all covered by the same defenders, so nobody surprises anyone.
karty.rk: how many alternate routes; how hidden, narrow or long they are compared with the main route
karty.ik: <rect x="24" y="24" width="16" height="16" rx="2" fill="#2f6b8f"/><path d="M6 58V34c0-14 10-24 24-24h14" stroke-dasharray="2 7"/><path d="M44 10l-8-5v10z" fill="#e85d4f" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M32 58V44" stroke-width="5"/><path d="M54 20v38" stroke="#d5d9e0" stroke-width="6"/>

karty.g: The last turn of one round and the first of the next go to the same player.
karty.nz: The turn order must change between rounds, and players need actions (like claiming first-player spot) that let them end one round and start the next. Without such player-driven control it happens only by accident.
karty.yr: Turn order shifts on paper, but nobody can steer it, so the back-to-back turn is a random side effect nobody plans for.
karty.rk: how turn order is reassigned; how much players can influence who goes first next round

karty.g: World elements through which the player performs actions and decides how to use them.
karty.nz: Give players clear elements through which their actions affect the world, and decide how many there are and whether control can switch between them. The actions offered must really be tied to these elements.
karty.yr: A character model is on screen, but all commands act on the world globally, so the avatar is just decoration.
karty.rk: how many controllable entities; which actions each one provides; whether control can be switched
karty.ik: <path d="M10 50h44l-6-10H16z" fill="#d5d9e0"/><circle cx="32" cy="20" r="12"/><path d="M32 4v8M32 28v8M16 20h8M40 20h8"/><circle cx="32" cy="20" r="4" fill="#e85d4f" stroke="none"/>

karty.g: Unexplored or unseen parts of the world are hidden from the player.
karty.nz: Hide parts of the world and make player entities with limited sight ranges reveal them, so lacking information truly affects choices. Decide whether terrain and units are hidden separately and whether revealed areas re-hide.
karty.yr: A dark overlay exists, but the map and enemies are fully known or revealed at once, so it never limits decisions.
karty.rk: sight range of units; whether explored areas re-hide; separate fog for terrain versus units

karty.g: Choice feels rich but does not overwhelm with too many options or the need to prioritize.
karty.nz: Offer a small, clearly presented set of actions with limited resources, and open goals without forcing or timing them. Players must feel agency, not obligation or overload.
karty.yr: A menu lists lots of options, but a timer or forced objective pushes one path, so the freedom is only felt on the surface.
karty.rk: number of distinct action types; how strongly goals and time pressure are imposed
karty.ik: <rect x="6" y="6" width="52" height="52" rx="3"/><path d="M14 48c6-4 8-12 14-14s10 4 18-8" stroke="#2f6b8f" stroke-width="4"/><circle cx="46" cy="26" r="5" fill="#c9a24a"/><path d="M14 14h6M44 14h6" stroke-width="3"/>

karty.g: Players can move and change game elements outside of the rules.
karty.nz: Components must be physical or open to hand manipulation, with no automated enforcement, and the group must tolerate rule bending. A human or self-run setup is needed rather than a strict program.
karty.yr: The rulebook says players may adjust things, but software or a strict facilitator blocks any rule-breaking move.
karty.rk: how much the facilitator or software enforces rules; how easily components can be altered
karty.ik: <rect x="6" y="40" width="20" height="18" rx="2" fill="#c9a24a"/><path d="M32 52h26"/><circle cx="44" cy="16" r="6" fill="#e85d4f"/><path d="M14 40c0-14 12-24 24-24" stroke-dasharray="1 6"/><path d="M50 30c6 0 8 6 8 10l-6 8h-8l-6-10c0-4 6-4 8 0V24c0-3 4-3 4 0z" fill="#fff" stroke-width="3"/>

karty.g: A set of items given to a player to hand out to others as they see fit.
karty.nz: Periodically grant gift items with some randomness, and let players choose recipients, often limited to friends or neighbors. The gifts need to be useful so giving matters.
karty.yr: A gift button exists, but the items are worthless or automatically sent, so nobody chooses and nothing is exchanged socially.
karty.rk: how often gifts are granted; how random their contents are; who can receive them

karty.g: The player has several actions available, and each feels meaningful.
karty.nz: Provide options with visibly different and relevant effects, and let players see or believe their choices matter. Avoid a dominant best option.
karty.yr: Several options exist, but one is clearly best or all give the same result, so choosing changes nothing.
karty.rk: number of meaningful options; how different their outcomes are; how visible the effects are

karty.g: The game keeps a list of players who matter to each person so they are easier to find.
karty.nz: Provide ways to add, confirm and find friends, and tie services such as chat, invites and gifts to the list. Needs server infrastructure to track players.
karty.yr: A list screen exists, but it connects to no matching, chat or gifts, so it is just a contact book.
karty.rk: how friends are found and confirmed; what features are limited to friends; friendship levels
karty.ik: <rect x="12" y="6" width="40" height="52" rx="4" fill="#fff"/><circle cx="24" cy="20" r="4" fill="#2f6b8f"/><circle cx="24" cy="34" r="4" fill="#c9a24a"/><circle cx="24" cy="48" r="4" fill="#4fa83a"/><path d="M34 20h10M34 34h10M34 48h10" stroke-width="3"/>

karty.g: Attacks by members of the same team damage their own teammates.
karty.nz: Teams must exist, and damage rules must apply to allies, with real cost to hitting them. Players need to be in situations where stray hits are plausible.
karty.yr: Friendly Fire is switched on, but damage to allies is trivial or ranges are so short that nobody ever worries about it.
karty.rk: damage dealt to allies; area-of-effect size; whether the option is on at each difficulty

karty.g: Enjoyment when things are going badly but the player keeps fighting.
karty.nz: Real-time pressure, more demands than the player can comfortably handle, and difficulty rising with skill, while keeping success still possible. Failure must seem close but not certain.
karty.yr: The screen is busy with enemies and effects, but the game is easy or pausable, so there is no pressure to cope.
karty.rk: density and simultaneity of threats; difficulty ramp rate; time pressure

karty.g: The game bypasses its own calculation rules or makes hidden exceptions to them.
karty.nz: Someone must be able to override results, either secretly by a facilitator or via a scarce player resource, and it must be rare so effort still matters. Hidden use requires outcomes not being fully open.
karty.yr: The rulebook mentions bending outcomes, but dice are rolled openly and rules are enforced, so nobody ever fudges anything.
karty.rk: how often overrides are allowed; whether they are secret or a limited player resource
karty.ik: <rect x="8" y="16" width="34" height="34" rx="6" fill="#fff"/><circle cx="17" cy="25" r="2.5" fill="#2a2a2a"/><circle cx="33" cy="41" r="2.5" fill="#2a2a2a"/><circle cx="25" cy="33" r="2.5" fill="#2a2a2a"/><path d="M38 60l6-14 14-30 4 4-30 36z" fill="#d5d9e0" stroke-width="3" transform="translate(-6 -2)"/><path d="M46 52l10-10" stroke="#e85d4f" stroke-width="4"/>

karty.g: Different kinds of actions are assigned to different participants.
karty.nz: Give entities different abilities and make tasks too many for one to cover, so cooperation and division of labor is necessary. Limited gear slots or exclusive abilities force specialization.
karty.yr: Class names exist, but everyone can do everything equally well, so the roles are just labels.
karty.rk: how different abilities are between roles; how much one entity can cover alone; number of slots

karty.g: The player can still improve their own skills in this game.
karty.nz: Outcomes must depend on skill with room above average play, plus feedback that shows how well players did. Changing rules or rising challenge keeps the headroom open.
karty.yr: The game claims depth, but outcomes are mostly luck or skill caps quickly, so practice yields nothing.
karty.rk: skill ceiling; amount of performance feedback; how outcome depends on skill versus luck
karty.ik: <path d="M6 58h52"/><path d="M8 58v-8h12v8M20 58V40h12v18M32 58V30h12v28" fill="#c9a24a"/><path d="M44 58V20h12v38" fill="#d5d9e0" stroke-dasharray="3 4"/><path d="M44 12l6-8 6 8" stroke="#4fa83a" stroke-width="4"/>

karty.g: Goal: learn to perform a certain skill in the game at the required level.
karty.nz: Offer abilities players can obtain through items, levels or upgrades, with real gameplay effects and a choice of paths. Players need a reason to want more power.
karty.yr: Upgrades exist but only give tiny or cosmetic bonuses, so nobody pursues them.
karty.rk: number and size of upgrades; cost to obtain; how many paths to choose

karty.g: Goal: act so as to obtain information and draw conclusions from it.
karty.nz: Hide information that matters for decisions, and give actions to uncover it. The knowledge must change what players do.
karty.yr: Players can discover facts, but the facts are irrelevant or already obvious, so searching has no use.
karty.rk: how much is hidden; cost and means of uncovering it; how useful the information is
karty.ik: <path d="M8 6h24l10 10v40H8z"/><path d="M32 6v10h10"/><path d="M14 24h16M14 32h12"/><circle cx="38" cy="40" r="11" fill="#c9a24a" fill-opacity=".45"/><path d="M46 48l12 12" stroke-width="6"/>

karty.g: Goal: become the owner of a certain game element.
karty.nz: Make ownership of items, pieces or areas matter, giving benefits, points or progress, and make it contestable. Without contest or reward it is just a pickup.
karty.yr: Players can own things, but ownership gives no benefit and nobody can take it, so there is no pursuit.
karty.rk: value of owned elements; how contestable they are; how many can be owned
karty.ik: <path d="M12 58V6"/><path d="M12 8h34l-8 10 8 10H12" fill="#e85d4f"/><path d="M6 58h24"/><circle cx="48" cy="48" r="9" fill="#c9a24a"/><path d="M48 44v8M44 48h8" stroke-width="3"/>

karty.g: Raised platforms from which narrow passages are easy to keep in view.
karty.nz: Build elevated positions overlooking a narrow route that enemies must follow for some distance, with height giving a real advantage. Alternate routes can offset the advantage.
karty.yr: There is a raised ledge, but the enemy can bypass it or it gives no combat edge, so the height means nothing.
karty.rk: height and length of the overlook; availability of flanking routes; cover
karty.ik: <path d="M4 56h56"/><path d="M4 20h56v8H4z" fill="#d5d9e0"/><path d="M10 28v28M22 28v28M42 28v28M54 28v28"/><circle cx="32" cy="10" r="5" fill="#2f6b8f"/><path d="M32 46l0-8" stroke="#e85d4f" stroke-width="4"/>

karty.g: A surface where it is easy to move elements and keep track of their positions relative to each other.
karty.nz: The layout must carry spatial relations that matter to the rules, such as movement, regions and positions. It should organize components the game needs.
karty.yr: A board is included, but it is just a backdrop; positions on it have no rule effect.
karty.rk: size and layout; number and type of regions; connections between spaces
karty.ik: <rect x="6" y="6" width="52" height="52" rx="3"/><path d="M6 32h52M32 6v52"/><rect x="6" y="6" width="26" height="26" fill="#d5d9e0"/><rect x="32" y="32" width="26" height="26" fill="#d5d9e0"/><circle cx="45" cy="19" r="5" fill="#e85d4f"/>

karty.g: New game elements are added to a game already in progress.
karty.nz: Define what can be inserted, when, and by whom, and let the new elements really change the situation. Who controls the insertion shapes pacing and surprise.
karty.yr: New things appear, but they are the same as before or too weak to matter, so nothing changes.
karty.rk: what is inserted; how often; who controls the insertion

karty.g: Players exchange, in real life, the items that make up the game.
karty.nz: Players must own different tradable items that keep value beyond one session, and be able to meet or exchange them. Item rarity and sources shape demand.
karty.yr: Items are labelled tradable, but all are equal or worthless, so nobody wants to swap.
karty.rk: rarity of items; how they are obtained; how easy trading is

karty.g: Stories based on the events of one particular game that was played.
karty.nz: Games need chances for remarkable, varied events, and ways to record or share them, such as replays. Exceptional or failure moments help.
karty.yr: A replay or save feature exists, but games unfold the same each time, so nothing worth telling comes out.
karty.rk: variance of events; ability to record and share; frequency of dramatic moments

karty.g: Objects inside the game world that can be carried or used.
karty.nz: Each item should have identity and an effect or use that matters, and be carried, found or moved. Different agents may use them differently.
karty.yr: Items are collectable, but all do the same or nothing, so picking them up changes nothing.
karty.rk: types and effects of items; how scarce they are; whether they wear out or can be dropped
karty.ik: <path d="M24 30c0-10 16-10 16 0" /><rect x="12" y="30" width="40" height="28" rx="6" fill="#c9a24a"/><path d="M12 42h40"/><rect x="28" y="38" width="8" height="8" rx="2" fill="#fff" stroke-width="3"/>

karty.g: A place where players gather before a game starts.
karty.nz: Provide a place to find players and games, choose settings, and communicate before starting. It needs server infrastructure and communication tools.
karty.yr: A lobby screen exists, but it only auto-assigns players with no choice or talk, so it is just a loading screen.
karty.rk: lobby scope; communication tools; filters and matchmaking options
karty.ik: <path d="M6 58V28l26-20 26 20v30z" fill="#d5d9e0"/><path d="M24 58V40h16v18" fill="#c9a24a"/><circle cx="15" cy="46" r="3" fill="#2f6b8f"/><circle cx="49" cy="46" r="3" fill="#e85d4f"/>

karty.g: People who run the game world and the players' interaction with it.
karty.nz: Give one participant the authority to run the world, adjudicate and improvise, backed by tools such as scenarios and rules. Players must accept their rulings.
karty.yr: A GM role is named, but it only reads out fixed text and cannot adapt anything, so it is a narrator.
karty.rk: how much authority and freedom the GM has; tools provided; whether the role rotates

karty.g: An event after which the player can no longer take part in the game.
karty.nz: Define clear triggers such as losing lives or elimination, with real exclusion from play. The risk must be credible.
karty.yr: A Game Over screen appears, but the player instantly resumes with no loss, so there is no exclusion.
karty.rk: what triggers it; how easily it can be reached; whether and how play can resume
karty.ik: <circle cx="32" cy="26" r="18" fill="#fff"/><path d="M20 52h24v8H20z"/><path d="M22 24l8 8M30 24l-8 8M36 24l8 8M44 24l-8 8" stroke="#e85d4f" stroke-width="4"/><path d="M26 44h12"/>

karty.g: A deliberate halt to the flow of game time and events.
karty.nz: Game time must otherwise run on its own, and the pause must truly stop events, possibly with limits or saving. It must be available at useful moments.
karty.yr: A pause button exists, but the game keeps running or it is blocked in tense moments, so it can't be used.
karty.rk: when pausing is allowed; maximum pause length; what remains active during it
karty.ik: <rect x="8" y="8" width="48" height="48" rx="8"/><rect x="20" y="20" width="8" height="24" rx="2" fill="#2f6b8f"/><rect x="36" y="20" width="8" height="24" rx="2" fill="#2f6b8f"/>

karty.g: Computers or mechanisms on which each separate play of the game runs.
karty.nz: Implement the rules and let players join and leave instances reliably, handling non-player actions and state. Stability and scale shape what is possible.
karty.yr: A server is mentioned, but the logic really runs on clients, so it adds no mediation or consistency.
karty.rk: players per server; persistence of the world; rule enforcement versus simulation

karty.g: An indicator, not the game world itself, tells about the game or other players.
karty.nz: Show information players really need, in a form they can read quickly and tied to decisions. Choose what is shown beyond what the avatar could sense.
karty.yr: An indicator is on screen, but it shows something irrelevant or duplicates what is already obvious.
karty.rk: what is displayed; update speed and prominence; diegetic versus non-diegetic
karty.ik: <path d="M8 46a24 24 0 0 1 48 0z" fill="#fff"/><path d="M14 40a18 18 0 0 1 8-10" stroke="#4fa83a" stroke-width="4"/><path d="M42 30a18 18 0 0 1 8 10" stroke="#e85d4f" stroke-width="4"/><path d="M32 46L42 24"/><path d="M6 54h52"/>

karty.g: Information that gives more than you can see just by looking at the game elements.
karty.nz: Collect scattered information into views such as maps or panels that support planning, and make them accurate and easy to read. They should show things players can't see directly.
karty.yr: An overview screen exists, but it shows only what is visible anyway or is too cluttered to use.
karty.rk: what information is included; level of detail; how accessible it is during play
karty.ik: <rect x="6" y="8" width="52" height="40" rx="3"/><path d="M6 28l14-8 14 8 12-6 12 6"/><rect x="34" y="14" width="16" height="12" fill="#c9a24a" fill-opacity=".6" stroke-width="3"/><path d="M22 56h20M32 48v8"/>

karty.g: A passive participant controlled by the system under simple rules, with no visible will.
karty.nz: Give it simple fixed rules players can understand and perform, with enough power to actually threaten them. Its actions should be easy to carry out in self-run games.
karty.yr: A dummy opponent exists but can't affect the outcome, so it is just scenery.
karty.rk: how complex its rules are; how strong its actions are; how much randomness it uses
karty.ik: <rect x="14" y="18" width="36" height="30" rx="6" fill="#d5d9e0"/><path d="M32 18V8"/><circle cx="32" cy="6" r="3" fill="#e85d4f"/><circle cx="24" cy="32" r="4" fill="#2f6b8f"/><circle cx="40" cy="32" r="4" fill="#2f6b8f"/><path d="M24 56h16M20 48v8M44 48v8"/>

karty.g: A player is removed from the game early as a punishment while the others' game continues.
karty.nz: Elimination must really remove the player from play, with no cheap way back (no free continues, easy rejoin or endless extra chances). The trigger, such as losing the last life or health hitting zero, must be clear and plausibly threatening.
karty.yr: A 'Game Over' screen that drops you back a few seconds earlier with everything kept, so nothing is actually lost.
karty.rk: what triggers elimination; how easy it is to rejoin or continue
karty.ik: <rect x="8" y="12" width="36" height="28" rx="3"/><path d="M18 22l12 8M30 22l-12 8" stroke="#e85d4f" stroke-width="4"/><path d="M14 50h24M26 40v10"/><path d="M46 28h12v-6M46 28a12 12 0 0 0 12 12" stroke-width="3"/><path d="M52 50l6 6" stroke-width="3"/>

karty.g: Actions by which the player changes the flow of game time.
karty.nz: The game must have a state and timeline that can really be paused, sped up, slowed or rewound, and the ability must cost something or be limited. In multiplayer, decide whose time is affected so others keep their agency.
karty.yr: A rewind or slow-motion button so cheap, or so rarely needed, that nobody changes decisions because of it, or a visual slowdown that changes nothing in the rules.
karty.rk: which time effects exist (stop, slow, fast, reverse); how often and at what cost they can be used
karty.ik: <circle cx="32" cy="32" r="24" fill="#fff"/><path d="M32 16v16l10 6"/><path d="M6 14l-2 12 12-2" stroke="#2f6b8f" stroke-width="4"/><path d="M6 26C8 14 18 6 32 6" stroke="#2f6b8f" stroke-width="4"/>

karty.g: Goal: learn how the game world is laid out or find a needed place or item in it.
karty.nz: Players must not see the whole world at once, and they must have real choices about where to go. Something worth finding, such as secrets, resources or shortcuts, must be spread across the unknown areas.
karty.yr: A big map where everything is already shown or marked, or where the path is a single corridor, so 'exploring' is just walking.
karty.rk: how much of the world is hidden; how much is hidden and where rewards are placed; how much help (maps, clues) is given
karty.ik: <rect x="6" y="8" width="52" height="48" rx="3"/><path d="M14 46c6-10 14-4 18-14s12-8 16-14" stroke-dasharray="1 7"/><circle cx="14" cy="46" r="3" fill="#2a2a2a"/><path d="M44 12l8 8M52 12l-8 8" stroke="#e85d4f"/>

karty.g: Finding a way from one place in the game world to another when the route is not obvious.
karty.nz: Need a world with several possible routes and no obvious best one, so wrong turns are possible, and a destination worth reaching. Navigation aids must not give the answer away.
karty.yr: A level with a single path, or a minimap and waypoint line that always shows where to go, so there is nothing to work out.
karty.rk: how many routes and branches; how strong the navigation aids are (map, markers, landmarks)
karty.ik: <circle cx="32" cy="32" r="24"/><path d="M32 14l8 18-8 18-8-18z" fill="#e85d4f" stroke-width="3"/><path d="M32 32l-8 0 8-18z" fill="#fff" stroke-width="3"/><circle cx="32" cy="32" r="2.5" fill="#2a2a2a" stroke="none"/>

karty.g: Fictional worlds in which the game takes place.
karty.nz: The world must actually define where things are and how they move or interact, with boundaries and rules that tie into the actions. The fiction should explain and support the rules, not sit apart from them.
karty.yr: A fictional setting used only as wallpaper or a title, while the rules would work the same on a plain grid.
karty.rk: size and boundaries; continuous vs discrete space; what elements and resources are placed in it

karty.g: A structure the player builds so that it works for them.
karty.nz: Players need to be able to build components that feed each other so output grows (positive feedback, combos), with several possible builds to choose from. There must be a payoff, such as a scoring phase, that makes the engine worth the investment.
karty.yr: Upgrades that are just flat bonuses and do not interact or compound, so there is no engine to build, only a list of purchases.
karty.rk: how strongly parts reinforce each other; cost and speed of building; when and how scoring starts

karty.g: The ability to perform actions and reach goals in the game with confidence.
karty.nz: Skill must matter: outcomes depend on player choices and execution more than luck, with consistent rules, readable feedback and challenge that is reachable but keeps pushing. There must be room to improve over repeated play.
karty.yr: A game where results are mostly random or one dominant strategy wins, so 'getting better' is not real, or levelling up that does the work for the player.
karty.rk: balance of skill vs luck; difficulty and learning curve; depth and complexity of the rules

karty.g: Records of values and events that can be viewed during or after the game.
karty.nz: The game must track meaningful events or values and make them reachable by players during or after play, and players must care about them, for example to compare or review. Presentation should be readable and persistent.
karty.yr: A stats screen full of numbers that nobody looks at or can use, or records that are lost as soon as the session ends.
karty.rk: what is recorded; how long it is kept and who can see it
karty.ik: <rect x="6" y="8" width="52" height="48" rx="3"/><path d="M16 48V36M28 48V24M40 48V30M50 48V16" stroke="#2f6b8f" stroke-width="7"/><path d="M10 52h44"/>

karty.g: The player sees the game as a system of rules and looks for winning tricks in it.
karty.nz: The game needs to make effort feel worthwhile and the player absorbed, with clear goals and feedback so they willingly commit and treat play as serious. The page is a stub, so this is inferred from the patterns it lists.
karty.yr: Labelling a mode or menu option 'gamer' or 'hardcore' without any change in challenge, stakes or engagement.
karty.rk: how much effort the game demands and how clearly that effort is rewarded

karty.g: Enemies that cannot be told apart from one another.
karty.nz: One template spawned in numbers, simple enough to be interchangeable, with a defined spawn timing and place. Some small random variation or loot variety helps stop them feeling flat.
karty.yr: Enemies that look different (new skins or names) but behave and fight exactly the same, or a single 'crowd' that never poses a threat.
karty.rk: how many appear and how often they spawn; how strong they are; how much variation is allowed

karty.g: With each step of effort, the result is multiplied by the same factor.
karty.nz: A clear multiplier applied to a cost, reward or effect, with a ratio above or below 1 chosen on purpose. The numbers must be large enough that players notice the growth or decay and change how they invest.
karty.yr: A ratio so close to 1 or with such low starting values that the growth is invisible, so it plays like a flat linear increase.
karty.rk: the common ratio; the starting value; where in the game it is applied (costs, rewards, scores)
karty.ik: <path d="M6 56h52"/><rect x="8" y="50" width="6" height="6" fill="#c9a24a" stroke-width="3"/><rect x="18" y="46" width="8" height="10" fill="#c9a24a" stroke-width="3"/><rect x="30" y="38" width="10" height="18" fill="#c9a24a" stroke-width="3"/><rect x="44" y="8" width="12" height="48" fill="#e85d4f" stroke-width="3"/>

karty.g: Interface elements tied to a place in the world but not part of it.
karty.nz: Information must be attached to a location or object in the world, positioned so it is seen when needed, and it should actually help players decide something. Accept that it breaks the fiction.
karty.yr: A marker or label that repeats what is already obvious on screen, or one placed in a HUD corner far from the thing it describes.
karty.rk: what information is shown; where and when it appears; whether it shows through walls or only in view

karty.g: Records of players' past attempts, including your own, become opponents in a new game.
karty.nz: The game must record player actions and replay them in the same setup so the ghost's performance can be compared directly. Decide whether ghosts affect the player and whose runs get saved, and the setting needs a clear measure such as time or score.
karty.yr: A ghost that is always the same fixed, designer-made run, or one that is shown but has no way to compare or race, so there is nothing at stake against it.
karty.rk: whose runs are saved and how they are chosen; whether the ghost can affect the player; whether runs are shared
karty.ik: <path d="M10 56V26a16 16 0 0 1 32 0v30l-5-5-5 5-6-5-5 5-6-5z" fill="#fff" fill-opacity=".6" stroke-dasharray="4 5"/><path d="M20 28h0M32 28h0" stroke-width="5"/><path d="M46 56V40M46 40l12 4-12 6" fill="#e85d4f" stroke-width="3"/>

karty.g: Goal: complete a game task in order to earn an achievement reward.
karty.nz: Goals must be real, challenging and require skill, and the achievements must be recorded persistently and, ideally, be visible to others. Difficulty must be high enough that getting one reflects mastery rather than luck or routine play.
karty.yr: A badge for something trivial or automatic, such as finishing the tutorial, which changes nothing about how people play.
karty.rk: which goals have achievements; how hard they are; who can see them

karty.g: Goal: goals are linked so that completing or failing some affects others.
karty.nz: Goals must really depend on each other, so finishing lower goals is needed for, or helps, higher ones. The relationships should be visible to players so they can plan around them.
karty.yr: A list of tasks that can all be done in any order with no effect on one another, just presented as a tree.
karty.rk: number of levels; how strict the dependencies are; whether lower goals are required or optional
